ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">vocal</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx50" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx50.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">    </span><span id="lstnumberx50.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">}</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx51" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx51.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">  </span><span id="lstnumberx51.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">],</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx52" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx52.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">  </span><span id="lstnumberx52.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"</span><span id="lstnumberx52.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">reading_order</span><span id="lstnumberx52.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">":</span><span id="lstnumberx52.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx52.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">["</span><span id="lstnumberx52.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">e1</span><span id="lstnumberx52.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"],</span><span id="lstnumberx52.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">                                  </span><span id="lstnumberx52.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">//</span><span id="lstnumberx52.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx52.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">documents</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx53" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx53.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">  </span><span id="lstnumberx53.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"</span><span id="lstnumberx53.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">global_description</span><span id="lstnumberx53.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">":</span><span id="lstnumberx53.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx53.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">{</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx54" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx54.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">    </span><span id="lstnumberx54.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"</span><span id="lstnumberx54.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">caption</span><span id="lstnumberx54.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">":</span><span id="lstnumberx54.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx54.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"...",</span><span id="lstnumberx54.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx54.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"</span><span id="lstnumberx54.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">narrative</span><span id="lstnumberx54.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">":</span><span id="lstnumberx54.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx54.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"...",</span><span id="lstnumberx54.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx54.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"</span><span id="lstnumberx54.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">scene</span><span id="lstnumberx54.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">":</span><span id="lstnumberx54.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx54.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"...",</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx55" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx55.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">    </span><span id="lstnumberx55.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"</span><span id="lstnumberx55.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">language</span><span id="lstnumberx55.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">":</span><span id="lstnumberx55.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx55.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"...",</span><span id="lstnumberx55.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx55.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"</span><span id="lstnumberx55.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">tag</span><span id="lstnumberx55.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">":</span><span id="lstnumberx55.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx55.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"..."</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx56" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx56.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">  </span><span id="lstnumberx56.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">},</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx57" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx57.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">  </span><span id="lstnumberx57.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"</span><span id="lstnumberx57.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">structured_report</span><span id="lstnumberx57.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">":</span><span id="lstnumberx57.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx57.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">"..."</span><span id="lstnumberx57.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">                               </span><span id="lstnumberx57.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">//</span><span id="lstnumberx57.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx57.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">text</span><span id="lstnumberx57.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">-</span><span id="lstnumberx57.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">rich</span><span id="lstnumberx57.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx57.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">video</span><span id="lstnumberx57.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">;</span><span id="lstnumberx57.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx57.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">empty</span><span id="lstnumberx57.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx57.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">for</span><span id="lstnumberx57.20" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx57.21" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">natural</span><span id="lstnumberx57.22" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx57.23" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">video</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx58" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx58.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">}</span>
</div>
</div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="listing1.12" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">List of listings 1</span> </span><span id="listing1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of the OmniSchema output.<span id="listing1.13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The listing is schematic: <span id="listing1.13.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">|</span> separates alternative values, <span id="listing1.13.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"..."</span> stands for elided content, and comments (<span id="listing1.13.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">//</span>) are annotations rather than part of the output. Each task uses the subset of fields it needs; comments mark the inputs that use a field, and an unmarked field applies to every input that uses its enclosing field. Every output has <span id="listing1.13.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">modality</span>, a list of <span id="listing1.13.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">elements</span> or <span id="listing1.13.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">segments</span>, and <span id="listing1.13.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">global_description</span>.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As discussed in Sec. <a href="#S1" title="1 Introduction ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, parsing results of different modalities share a common form: a set of units, each localized in space or time and paired with the content extracted from the corresponding region or interval.
Motivated by this observation, we design a unified output schema, OmniSchema, which covers ten parsing tasks across three modalities: images (document pages and natural images), audio, and video.
Because every element or segment is localized by an explicit spatial or temporal anchor, each parsed result is traceable to its source region or time interval.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Schema structure.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Lst. <a href="#listing1" title="List of listings 1 ‣ 3 Omni-Modal Parsing Schema ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> gives an overview of the schema.
Each output is serialized as a JSON object with three common required fields: <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">modality</span>, a list of localized units with their content (<span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">elements</span> for images, <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">segments</span> for audio and video), and a global description of the input (<span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">global_description</span>). Additional fields depend on the task: <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">subtype</span> and <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">reading_order</span> are included where applicable, and video outputs contain <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">structured_report</span>, populated for text-rich video and left empty for natural video.
The unit type depends on the modality.
For images, the unit is an <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">element</em>, a spatial region delimited by a bounding box <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;box&gt;&lt;x_1&gt;&lt;y_1&gt;&lt;x_2&gt;&lt;y_2&gt;&lt;/box&gt;</span> whose coordinates are normalized to <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> relative to the image width and height; for audio and video, it is a <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">segment</em>, a time interval delimited by start and end timestamps (<span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">HH:MM:SS</span>, i.e., at one-second resolution, relative to the input onset), and each speech segment additionally includes one speaker identifier that is consistent across the input.
The content fields of each unit contain the information extracted from the corresponding region or interval.
For example, <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">text</span> contains the recognized text of a text element, <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">otsl</span> encodes the structure and cell content of a table, and <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">asr_text</span> contains the speech transcript of an audio or video segment.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multi-task parsing.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Youtu-Parsing-Omni supports ten parsing tasks: on images, document parsing, chemical structure recognition, sheet music recognition, chart parsing, flowchart parsing, geometric figure parsing, and natural image parsing; on audio, audio parsing; and on video, natural video parsing and text-rich video parsing.
In the image tasks, each parsed region is an element delimited by a bounding box.
In <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">document parsing</em>, each element on the page is labeled with a layout category, placed in the reading order, and transcribed according to its category, e.g., as plain text, a <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_LaTeX_logo" style="letter-spacing:-0.2em; margin-right:0.1em;">L<span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="position:relative; bottom:0.4ex;font-variant:small-caps;;">a</span>T<span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="position:relative; bottom:-0.2ex;font-variant:small-caps;font-size:120%;">e</span>X</span> formula, or a table serialized in Optimized Table Structure Language (OTSL).
In <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">chemical structure recognition</em>, a molecule is parsed as a document element whose content is a SMILES <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite> string.
In <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">sheet music recognition</em>, a musical score is parsed as a document element whose content is ABC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite> notation.
In <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">chart parsing</em>, <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">flowchart parsing</em>, and <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">geometric figure parsing</em>, the whole figure forms a single element whose content is its underlying data as a Markdown table, its nodes and edges as a Mermaid graph, or its geometric primitives and their relations as a geometry string, respectively; the element also contains a caption.
In <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">natural image parsing</em>, each salient object forms an element with a bounding box, a tag naming the object, the text inside the box, and a region caption, and the global description adds an image caption, a narrative, and a scene description.
In the audio and video tasks, the input is divided into a sequence of time segments.
Each audio segment is labeled as vocal or nonvocal: a vocal segment contains a speaker identifier, a transcript, the language of the speech, acoustic-event labels, and captions of timbre, delivery, and scene, whereas a nonvocal segment contains acoustic-event labels and a caption of the acoustic environment.
Each video segment contains the objects and on-screen text visible in its frames, where each text item is labeled with an optical character recognition (OCR) type such as title.
It also contains atomic actions, actor-object interactions, camera motion at a coarse and a fine level, an event description, and the speaker identifier, transcript, and acoustic-event labels of the accompanying audio.
<em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.9" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Natural video parsing</em> and <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.10" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">text-rich video parsing</em> share this segment structure; the output of text-rich video parsing additionally contains a structured report in Markdown that summarizes the whole video, a field left empty for natural video.
Full example outputs for each input type are given in App. <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Qualitative Examples ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Token roles.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because every output follows OmniSchema, each token of a serialized output can be assigned one of two roles, which OSAD supervises with different objectives (Subsec. <a href="#S4.SS2.SSS3" title="4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2.3</span></a>).
Structure tokens belong to the JSON syntax, namely keys and punctuation such as braces, brackets, colons, and commas, and follow a constrained grammar; content tokens belong to field values, which can admit multiple valid continuations.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Training</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training first develops unified perception through four pre-training stages and then refines structured parsing through three post-training stages (Fig. <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).
Supervised fine-tuning establishes the output format and instruction following; two subsequent on-policy stages refine the model’s own parses using verifiable rewards and then reference-conditioned token-level supervision.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.39301v1/training_recipe.svg" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/120;" width="476" height="120"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S4.F5.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Perception first, output format second, on-policy refinement last.<span id="S4.F5.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Four pre-training stages (Stage 0: perception alignment; Stage 1: omni-modal pre-training; Stage 2: annealing; Stage 3: long-context extension) are followed by three post-training stages: supervised fine-tuning, schema-routed RLVR, and OSAD. Rows give each stage’s token budget, trainable parameters, sequence-length limit, number of encoder fusion layers, and maximum frames per training video. Stage 1 uses sequence lengths of <math id="S4.F5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> k–<math id="S4.F5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> k. LoRA denotes low-rank adaptation of frozen base weights.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Pre-Training</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Pre-training turns a text-only decoder and a text-initialized encoder into an omni-modal perceiver, which raises three coupled problems.
First, the randomly initialized stems and projectors must learn to map pixels and mel frames into a representation that the pre-trained Transformer weights can read.
Second, the model must acquire dense, native-resolution perception of images, audio, and video without eroding the decoder’s language ability.
Third, it must handle long inputs such as multi-page documents and long videos.
Addressing all three at once is both costly and unstable: gradients through randomly initialized projectors would perturb the pre-trained decoder, and long native-resolution sequences are expensive to train on before the features are aligned.
We therefore adopt a staged curriculum, and progressively expand four axes across Stages 0–3 (Fig. <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>):
the trainable parameters (encoder only, then all parameters);
the input scale (from <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> k-token sequences with at most <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math> tokens per image to <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> k-token sequences with up to <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>512</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512</annotation></semantics></math> video frames);
cross-modal interaction (from no fusion layers to four);
and input perturbation (from none to stochastic routing and augmentation).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We initialize the decoder from our text-only checkpoint and the shared encoder block from Qwen3-0.6B-Base <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite> without its embedding layer and LM head; stems and projectors are randomly initialized.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Stage 0: Perception Alignment.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The first stage bridges the randomly initialized stems and projectors to the pre-trained weights on either side of them.
Only the encoder (stems, shared block, and projectors) is trained, while the decoder stays frozen.
Freezing the decoder serves two purposes: it shields the language model from the noisy gradients of the new projectors, and it forces the encoder to produce features in the input space that the fixed language model already interprets.
The supervision is dense: captions and transcripts describe the whole input, so every region of an image and every second of a recording contributes to the loss, whereas a short answer about one region, as in visual question answering, would provide little supervision for the remaining content.
Inputs are kept small (at most <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math> tokens per image, <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> frames per video, and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> k tokens per sequence) and no fusion layer is enabled, so that alignment is learned cheaply over a large token budget before native-resolution inputs make each step expensive.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Stage 1: Omni-Modal Pre-Training.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Once the encoder emits features that the decoder can read, the bottleneck shifts from alignment to capacity: a frozen decoder cannot learn to emit the long, dense symbol sequences required by parsing.
Stage 1 therefore unfreezes all parameters and is the largest stage, consuming <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.28</annotation></semantics></math> T tokens.
The image budget grows from <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math> k tokens so that the model sees pages at native resolution, videos grow to <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> frames of up to <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>512</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512</annotation></semantics></math> tokens each, and sequence lengths range from <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> k to <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> k tokens.
Four fusion layers are enabled at this point, so that frames attend to the co-occurring audio (Subsec. <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Unified Positional Encoding and Audio-Visual Fusion ‣ 2 Model ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>) only after each modality has been aligned on its own.
Text-only data are mixed in to limit catastrophic forgetting of the decoder’s language ability.
The learning rate is held constant so the total budget need not be fixed in advance and any checkpoint can be handed to the decay stage.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Stage 2: Annealing.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under a constant learning rate, the loss plateaus above the level that a subsequent learning-rate decay reaches, and annealing is a standard final phase of large-scale pre-training.
Stage 2 decays the learning rate from <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> with a cosine schedule over <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>512</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512</annotation></semantics></math> B tokens, with sequences fixed at <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> k tokens and slightly larger image and per-frame budgets.
Because annealing consolidates what the model has learned, we also introduce two mechanisms here that protect or broaden the learned perception.
First, layer-wise learning-rate decay scales the learning rate of encoder depth <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{L+1-\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{L+1-\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.9</annotation></semantics></math>, from the stems (<math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell=0</annotation></semantics></math>) to the projectors (<math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell=L+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell=L+1</annotation></semantics></math>, no decay); the projectors, the newest components, keep adapting, whereas the stems and lower layers, which already encode generic low-level features, are protected from being overwritten.
Second, audio-visual videos are routed stochastically with fused-route probability <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{fus}}=0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>fus</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{fus}}=0.8</annotation></semantics></math>, so they take the independent route with probability <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.2</annotation></semantics></math> and both routes remain usable at inference.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Stage 3: Long-Context Extension.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multi-page documents and long videos require far longer sequences than Stages 0–2 provide.
Stage 3 trains on sequences of up to <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> k tokens, with up to <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="102{,}400" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>102,400</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">102{,}400</annotation></semantics></math> tokens per image or video and videos of up to <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>512</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512</annotation></semantics></math> frames, for <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> B tokens at a constant learning rate of <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Post-Training</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Pre-training yields a model that perceives all three modalities but does not yet emit OmniSchema reliably.
Post-training proceeds through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for OmniSchema serialization, schema-routed reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for sequence-level optimization, and OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation (OSAD) for token-adaptive supervision and iterative self-evolution.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.1 </span>Supervised Fine-Tuning</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Starting from the Stage 3 checkpoint, we train all parameters on prompt–response pairs to establish reliable OmniSchema serialization and instruction following.
Although the pre-training mixture already contains parsing data, the Stage 3 model does not yet consistently respond to a task prompt with a complete, schema-conformant object; SFT makes this output format the default response to each parsing instruction.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The SFT mixture combines two sources.
Parsing data cover all ten tasks in Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Omni-Modal Parsing Schema ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>: each sample pairs a task prompt and its image, audio, or video input with a reference parse serialized in OmniSchema, so a single model learns to emit the fields each task requires.
General-purpose data, reused from Youtu-LLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>, Youtu-VL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>, Long-VITA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>, VITA-1.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, and VITA-Audio <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>, span text-only, visual, and audio instructions and preserve the conversational and instruction-following abilities that a parsing-only mixture would erode.
SFT uses a budget of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> B tokens, sequences of up to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> k tokens, and at most <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> frames per video, and keeps the four fusion layers of Stages 1–3 (Fig. <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">SFT also prepares the model for the two on-policy stages that follow, both of which learn from the model’s own rollouts.
RLVR assigns zero reward to undecodable outputs, and with group-mean-centered advantages, a group in which every rollout fails yields no gradient; OSAD likewise distills only from rollouts that pass its admission checks.
A policy that rarely produces well-formed parses would therefore supply few useful learning signals to either stage.
SFT, however, supervises the model only under reference prefixes, a limitation that the on-policy stages address (Subsec. <a href="#S4.SS2.SSS3" title="4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.2 </span>Schema-Routed RLVR</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For an input query <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> denote the generated parse, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> its reference parse, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> the task index.
Here, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> includes the task prompt and its multimodal input.
We optimize the policy on its own generated parses with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>. The reward is gated by decodability and the presence of a primary payload, and combines shared well-formedness with task-specific content accuracy:</p>
<table id="S4.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_gather ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle R(y,y^{\star},\nu)=\mathds{1}[y\text{ decodes}]\,\mathds{1}[y\text{ has a payload}]\cdot\mathrm{clip}_{[0,1]}\big(\Omega(y,y^{\star})\cdot\mathrm{core}_{\nu}(y,y^{\star})\big)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> decodes</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_double-struck" mathvariant="double-struck"> 1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> has a payload</mtext></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>clip</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>core</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle R(y,y^{\star},\nu)=\mathds{1}[y\text{ decodes}]\,\mathds{1}[y\text{ has a payload}]\cdot\mathrm{clip}_{[0,1]}\big(\Omega(y,y^{\star})\cdot\mathrm{core}_{\nu}(y,y^{\star})\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S4.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\Omega(y,y^{\star})=\mathrm{Fmt}(y)\,\big(1-0.6\,P_{\mathrm{repeat}}\big)\,\big(1-0.7\,P_{\mathrm{under}}\big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Fmt</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>0.6</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>repeat</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>0.7</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>under</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\Omega(y,y^{\star})=\mathrm{Fmt}(y)\,\big(1-0.6\,P_{\mathrm{repeat}}\big)\,\big(1-0.7\,P_{\mathrm{under}}\big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The indicator <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathds{1}[\cdot]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>𝟙</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathds{1}[\cdot]</annotation></semantics></math> equals one when its condition holds and zero otherwise; <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{clip}_{[0,1]}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>clip</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{clip}_{[0,1]}</annotation></semantics></math> restricts its argument to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.
If either gate fails, the reward is zero; otherwise, it equals the clipped product of the well-formedness and content factors. Thus the final reward lies in <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.
The shared factor <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega</annotation></semantics></math> combines schema validity, scored by <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Fmt}(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Fmt</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Fmt}(y)</annotation></semantics></math>, with penalties for repetition (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{repeat}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>repeat</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{repeat}}</annotation></semantics></math>) and incomplete coverage (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{under}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>under</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{under}}</annotation></semantics></math>).
Both penalties compare <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>; their arguments are suppressed for brevity, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math> are their respective coefficients.
The task-specific factor <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{core}_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>core</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{core}_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math> averages grounded-field accuracy and reference-description similarity when reference descriptions are available; otherwise, it uses grounded-field accuracy alone.
App. <a href="#A3.SS1" title="C.1 Schema-Routed RLVR ‣ Appendix C Post-Training Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a> details the validity checks, penalties, and task-specific scorers.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.3 </span>OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation</h4>

<figure id="S4.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.39301v1/osad_mech_figure.png" id="S4.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/299;" width="476" height="299" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S4.F6.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">OSAD combines token-adaptive on-policy supervision with teacher refresh at each round boundary.<span id="S4.F6.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Admitted student rollouts provide shared prefixes for a LoRA-trained student and a frozen, reference-conditioned teacher. The objective combines content-specific JS divergence at <math id="S4.F6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{c}</annotation></semantics></math>, structure-specific forward KL divergence at <math id="S4.F6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, and an all-token JS term at <math id="S4.F6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. Within each round, only the student’s adapters are updated. At the round boundary, the learned adapters are merged into the base weights to initialize the next teacher and student; the student receives fresh adapters, while only the teacher conditions on the reference. The lower panel illustrates the update and refresh mechanism rather than a measured model-state distance.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Starting from the RLVR checkpoint, OSAD refines generated parses through token-adaptive supervision and self-evolution through teacher refresh (Fig. <a href="#S4.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>).
The first matches supervision to each token’s schema role; the second updates the teacher as the student learns.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Token-adaptive on-policy supervision.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SFT trains on reference prefixes, whereas inference uses model-generated prefixes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>, <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>.
RLVR trains on these generated prefixes but assigns one reward to the entire parse.
OSAD complements this sequence-level optimization with reference-conditioned targets at each token, building on on-policy distillation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>, <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite> and reference-conditioned self-distillation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>, with the reference serving as privileged information <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">OSAD proceeds in rounds. Within round <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, a frozen teacher with parameters <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\theta}_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\theta}_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> and a student with effective parameters <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> start from the same checkpoint.
The student trains low-rank adapters (LoRA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite> on frozen base weights and samples a response <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{T})</annotation></semantics></math> of length <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> for each query <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.
Only rollouts passing JSON-validity, schema-conformance, box-syntax, and repetition checks enter distillation; rejected rollouts are masked (App. <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ Appendix C Post-Training Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a>).
Both models score the same generated prefix <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{&lt;t}=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{t-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{&lt;t}=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{t-1})</annotation></semantics></math>, but only the teacher receives the reference parse through <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{x}=[y^{\star};x]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>;</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{x}=[y^{\star};x]</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S4.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}^{(\tau)}=\mathrm{softmax}\big(f_{\theta}(x,y_{&lt;t})/\tau\big),\qquad q_{t}^{(\tau)}=\mathrm{softmax}\big(f_{\bar{\theta}_{r}}(\tilde{x},y_{&lt;t})/\tau\big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>r</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}^{(\tau)}=\mathrm{softmax}\big(f_{\theta}(x,y_{&lt;t})/\tau\big),\qquad q_{t}^{(\tau)}=\mathrm{softmax}\big(f_{\bar{\theta}_{r}}(\tilde{x},y_{&lt;t})/\tau\big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Here, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}^{(\tau)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}^{(\tau)}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}^{(\tau)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}^{(\tau)}</annotation></semantics></math> are student and teacher next-token distributions, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> returns vocabulary logits, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> denotes distillation temperature.
Shared prefixes thus provide aligned targets on the student’s own trajectories without exposing the reference to the student.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Following the token roles in Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Omni-Modal Parsing Schema ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, let <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}(y)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(y)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the content and structure positions of a response, respectively.
Content fields may admit several valid continuations, whereas JSON keys and punctuation follow a constrained grammar.
We therefore use the symmetric, bounded Jensen–Shannon (JS) divergence for content and the forward Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence for structure:</p>
<table id="S4.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="d_{t}^{\mathcal{C}}=\mathrm{JS}\big(q_{t}^{(\tau_{c})}\,\big\|\,p_{t}^{(\tau_{c})}\big),\qquad d_{t}^{\mathcal{S}}=\mathrm{KL}\big(q_{t}^{(\tau_{s})}\,\big\|\,p_{t}^{(\tau_{s})}\big),\qquad\tau_{s}&gt;\tau_{c}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>JS</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="1.200em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="1.200em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{t}^{\mathcal{C}}=\mathrm{JS}\big(q_{t}^{(\tau_{c})}\,\big\|\,p_{t}^{(\tau_{c})}\big),\qquad d_{t}^{\mathcal{S}}=\mathrm{KL}\big(q_{t}^{(\tau_{s})}\,\big\|\,p_{t}^{(\tau_{s})}\big),\qquad\tau_{s}&gt;\tau_{c}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">The per-position divergences <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{t}^{\mathcal{C}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{t}^{\mathcal{C}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{t}^{\mathcal{S}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{t}^{\mathcal{S}}</annotation></semantics></math> use content and structure temperatures <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively, and are computed over the full vocabulary. Round indices on temperatures and role weights are omitted here for brevity.
JS bounds content disagreement, while forward KL encourages coverage of the teacher’s structural predictions, softened by the higher structure temperature.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The objective combines a shared all-token term with additional role-specific terms.
For each nonempty role <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}\in\{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{S}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}\in\{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{S}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, define its mean divergence as <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{d}^{\,\mathcal{R}}(y)=|\mathcal{R}(y)|^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{R}(y)}d_{t}^{\mathcal{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{d}^{\,\mathcal{R}}(y)=|\mathcal{R}(y)|^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{R}(y)}d_{t}^{\mathcal{R}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The all-token term applies JS uniformly at temperature <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> and averages over all <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> response positions:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="d_{t}^{\mathrm{all}}=\mathrm{JS}\big(q_{t}^{(\tau)}\,\big\|\,p_{t}^{(\tau)}\big),\qquad\bar{d}^{\,\mathrm{all}}(y)=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}d_{t}^{\mathrm{all}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>all</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>JS</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="1.200em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>all</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>all</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{t}^{\mathrm{all}}=\mathrm{JS}\big(q_{t}^{(\tau)}\,\big\|\,p_{t}^{(\tau)}\big),\qquad\bar{d}^{\,\mathrm{all}}(y)=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}d_{t}^{\mathrm{all}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">With nonnegative content and structure weights <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, the per-rollout loss and minibatch objective are</p>
<table id="S4.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{row}}(y)=\frac{\bar{d}^{\,\mathrm{all}}(y)+\alpha_{c}\,\bar{d}^{\,\mathcal{C}}(y)+\alpha_{s}\,\bar{d}^{\,\mathcal{S}}(y)}{1+\alpha_{c}+\alpha_{s}},\qquad\mathcal{L}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{B}^{+}|}\sum_{y\in\mathcal{B}^{+}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{row}}(y)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>row</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>all</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4.3" class="ltx_p">Here, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> contains all admitted rollout instances in the global minibatch across data-parallel ranks; updates are skipped when this global collection is empty.
For an absent role, its weighted loss and coefficient are omitted from the numerator and denominator, respectively.
The all-token mean weights response positions equally, while role averaging controls the additional supervision independently of role length. Averaging over rollouts gives each admitted response equal weight. The role-weight schedule is given in App. <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ Appendix C Post-Training Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Self-evolution through teacher refresh.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Token-adaptive supervision remains tied to the starting checkpoint if the teacher stays fixed throughout training.
At each round boundary, OSAD merges the learned adapters into the student’s base weights to obtain <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>, which initializes the next teacher and student:</p>
<table id="S4.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\theta}_{r+1}\leftarrow\operatorname{stopgrad}(\theta_{r}),\qquad\theta_{\mathrm{init}}^{(r+1)}\leftarrow\bar{\theta}_{r+1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>stopgrad</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>init</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\theta}_{r+1}\leftarrow\operatorname{stopgrad}(\theta_{r}),\qquad\theta_{\mathrm{init}}^{(r+1)}\leftarrow\bar{\theta}_{r+1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Here, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{stopgrad}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>stopgrad</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{stopgrad}</annotation></semantics></math> blocks gradients, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{\mathrm{init}}^{(r+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>init</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{\mathrm{init}}^{(r+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the next student’s initial base weights, to which fresh low-rank adapters are added.
Teacher parameters are fixed within each round and refreshed between rounds, while reference conditioning remains exclusive to the teacher.
This alternation updates both the parser and its supervision on a fixed source pool.
We run six rounds of OSAD. App. <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Post-Training Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a> provides the training settings and pseudocode (Alg. <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ C.2 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ Appendix C Post-Training Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>); Subsec. <a href="#S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3" title="Contribution of OSAD. ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.7</span></a> evaluates the successive checkpoints.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T1.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 1</span>: </span><span id="S4.T1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Evaluation protocol.<span id="S4.T1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Size is the number of evaluated samples.
