<td id="S4.T2.9.1.28.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.5pt;padding-right:4.5pt;"><span id="S4.T2.9.1.28.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#EDEDED;">0.1104</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Evaluation</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate a single checkpoint under a single inference configuration and organize the evaluation around two questions: what this checkpoint achieves across modalities, and how the two ideas behind the model, the text-initialized unified encoder and self-evolving post-training, contribute.
Subsec. <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Setup ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a> describes the benchmarks, baselines, and protocol, and Subsec. <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 OmniDocBench v1.6 ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>–<a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 ChemOCR and PDMX-Synth ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a> report the results on each benchmark.
Subsec. <a href="#S5.SS7" title="5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.7</span></a> then studies the two principles of the encoder, one set of shared weights and initialization from a language model, in a controlled setting, and measures the contribution of self-evolving post-training on the final model.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Setup</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Benchmarks and baselines.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tab. <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Self-evolution through teacher refresh. ‣ 4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> lists every benchmark with its size, its metric, and the source of the baseline numbers.
OmniDocBench v1.6 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite> evaluates page-level document parsing; its Overall score averages text accuracy (<math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\text{edit distance}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mtext>edit distance</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\text{edit distance}</annotation></semantics></math>), formula CDM, and table TEDS.
PureDocBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> evaluates identical pages in clean, digitally degraded, and physically recaptured tracks, which isolates the cost of input degradation; it reports an Overall score per track and their mean, Avg<sub id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sub">3</sub>.
OmniParsingBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite> evaluates parsing of natural images, charts, geometry, audio, natural video, and text-rich video; each split is scored by a <em id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Perception</em> component over grounded fields, including localization, element extraction, OCR, and automatic speech recognition (ASR), and by a <em id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Cognition</em> component from multiple-choice questions that an LLM judge answers by reading only the parse.
Overall is the per-split leaderboard score: the mean of Perception and Cognition multiplied by the post-repair parse rate (Tab. <a href="#S5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 5.4 OmniParsingBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>–<a href="#S5.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ Graphics chart and geometry. ‣ 5.4 OmniParsingBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>).
On OmniParsingBench, every system is run and scored by us: we compare with the parsing-specialized Logics-Parsing-Omni, the open-weight generalists Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite> and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib66" title="" class="ltx_ref">66</a>]</cite>, and the API models Gemini-3-Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib62" title="" class="ltx_ref">62</a>]</cite> and GPT-5.4 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib67" title="" class="ltx_ref">67</a>]</cite>; Qwen3.5 and GPT-5.4 are evaluated only on image splits because neither model accepts audio input.
Video-MME-v2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite> evaluates general video understanding with <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{,}200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3,200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{,}200</annotation></semantics></math> multiple-choice questions arranged in groups of four; its group score rewards answering the related questions of a group consistently, and it is also reported for three capability levels (L1–L3). We use its setting without subtitles, in which models receive visual frames only.
ChemOCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite> evaluates chemical structure recognition from molecule images to SMILES, scored by the mean Tanimoto similarity of molecular fingerprints (Avg. Sim.) and the exact fingerprint-match rate (Tani@1.0).
PDMX-Synth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>, <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite> evaluates optical music recognition from rendered score images to ABC notation, scored by character, symbol, and line error rates (CER, SER, and LER).
For OmniDocBench, PureDocBench, and Video-MME-v2, the baseline numbers are taken from the official leaderboards; on ChemOCR and PDMX-Synth, we run every baseline with the official evaluator, except ChemDFM-X <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite> and LEGATO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, whose scores come from TinyChemVL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite> and LEGATO<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, respectively.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Protocol.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OmniDocBench, PureDocBench, Video-MME-v2, ChemOCR, and PDMX-Synth are scored with their official evaluation code or protocol.
OmniParsingBench is released without a complete evaluation toolkit, so we implement one from the metric definitions of the benchmark (App. <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Evaluation Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>) and re-score every system with it on one internal leaderboard.
These numbers, for our model and for every baseline, are thus comparable with each other, but not directly with those reported by the benchmark authors.
The toolkit repairs schema violations before scoring, so that formatting errors are not charged as content errors, and it uses corrected ground truth for a small number of verified annotation errors.
We set aside the camera-video subset because of annotation issues and exclude <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="136" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>136</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">136</annotation></semantics></math> samples with unavailable media, leaving <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{,}738" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3,738</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{,}738</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{,}874" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3,874</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{,}874</annotation></semantics></math> samples.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>OmniDocBench v1.6</h3>

<figure id="S5.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.39301v1/omnidocbench_analysis.svg" id="S5.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/163;" width="476" height="163"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="S5.F7.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Youtu-Parsing-Omni is the only model above <math id="S5.F7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96</annotation></semantics></math> on OmniDocBench v1.6 that also parses images, audio, and video, and its gain over Youtu-Parsing  comes mostly from tables and formulas.<span id="S5.F7.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
(a) OmniDocBench v1.6 Overall against total parameters (teal: open-weight), with API systems in a strip at the right; the document specialists at our level have <math id="S5.F7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.F7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.2</annotation></semantics></math> B parameters.
(b) Per-metric difference to Youtu-Parsing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>, our previous model, and to TeleOCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite>, the next-best system overall; edit distances are shown as <math id="S5.F7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\text{Edit}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mtext>Edit</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\text{Edit}</annotation></semantics></math> so that a positive difference always favors Youtu-Parsing-Omni.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first investigate whether broadening a model’s capabilities compromises its depth in document parsing, a domain in which specialized models are particularly strong.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The results indicate otherwise: while supporting a substantially broader range of input modalities and tasks, a single omni-modal model retains performance on par with specialized document parsers.
On OmniDocBench v1.6, Youtu-Parsing-Omni achieves the highest Overall score of <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.96</annotation></semantics></math> (Tab. <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Self-evolution through teacher refresh. ‣ 4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).
More importantly, this result does not rely on an isolated advantage in any single metric, but instead reflects balanced parsing performance: the differences from TeleOCR on text, formulas, and tables are all within <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.21</annotation></semantics></math> points, while Youtu-Parsing-Omni attains the best reading-order accuracy (Fig. <a href="#S5.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 5.2 OmniDocBench v1.6 ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>b).
Compared with Youtu-Parsing, the improvements are concentrated on tables and formulas, with gains of <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.8</annotation></semantics></math> TEDS and <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.2</annotation></semantics></math> CDM, respectively.
Both content types require the model to recover their structure accurately and serialize it correctly.
This pattern suggests that the new model improves not only visual recognition, but also the organization of recognized content into coherent, structured outputs.
Notably, this specialist-level document parsing performance is delivered by the same model that processes natural images, audio, and video across ten tasks (Fig. <a href="#S5.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 5.2 OmniDocBench v1.6 ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>a).
Thus, the broader modality coverage is achieved without weakening document understanding or fine-grained parsing capabilities.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>PureDocBench</h3>

<figure id="S5.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T3.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 3</span>: </span><span id="S5.T3.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Comparison with existing document parsing models and proprietary models on PureDocBench under clean and degraded conditions.<span id="S5.T3.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">

<sup id="S5.T3.8.1.1" class="ltx_sup">†</sup>Proprietary model.
</span>Bold<span id="S5.T3.8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> and <span id="S5.T3.8.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">underline</span>: best and second best of each Overall column.
</span></span></figcaption>

<td id="S5.T4.8.9.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.5pt;padding-right:4.5pt;"><span id="S5.T4.8.9.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#EDEDED;">78.08</span></td>

</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate the model’s robustness to degradation introduced during acquisition on PureDocBench, which comprises clean, digitally degraded, and physically recaptured inputs.
Youtu-Parsing-Omni achieves the highest Avg<sub id="S5.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sub">3</sub> among end-to-end models (<math id="S5.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76.29" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>76.29</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76.29</annotation></semantics></math>; Tab. <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 5.3 PureDocBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>) and outperforms every end-to-end specialist on all three tracks.
Its consistent lead over end-to-end specialists across both clean and degraded conditions indicates that the advantage stems from robust parsing rather than specialization to a particular acquisition condition.
Compared with Youtu-Parsing, Youtu-Parsing-Omni gains approximately <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> points on each of the three tracks.
The gains span all three component metrics and are more pronounced for formulas and tables, indicating that the model better preserves its ability to parse structured content under degradation rather than merely improving text recognition.
Nevertheless, most systems exhibit a marked performance decline on physically recaptured inputs, indicating that distortions and artifacts introduced during real-world acquisition remain a major challenge for document parsing.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Overall results.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next ask whether a single encoder can serve images, audio, and video at a competitive level, and where any advantage appears.
Under our evaluation toolkit, Youtu-Parsing-Omni is the strongest open-weight model on OmniParsingBench, with an average of <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75.08" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75.08</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75.08</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72.26" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>72.26</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72.26</annotation></semantics></math> for Logics-Parsing-Omni; among the models evaluated on every split, only the API model Gemini-3-Pro scores higher (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="77.44" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>77.44</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">77.44</annotation></semantics></math>; Tab. <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 5.3 PureDocBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, Fig. <a href="#S0.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>b).
It leads the other open-weight models on all three temporal splits (audio, natural video, and text-rich video) and attains the highest chart score of all systems (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>95.02</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95.02</annotation></semantics></math>).
The advantage, however, is not uniform across splits.
Relative to Logics-Parsing-Omni, Youtu-Parsing-Omni leads by <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.5</annotation></semantics></math> points on audio, <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.8</annotation></semantics></math> on natural video, and <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.3</annotation></semantics></math> on text-rich video (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.5</annotation></semantics></math> on average), whereas it trails by <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.8</annotation></semantics></math> points on average on the two static splits (natural images and graphics), mainly on natural images (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-4.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4.7</annotation></semantics></math>) and geometry (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-2.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2.0</annotation></semantics></math>).
These group means follow the leaderboard weighting, combining chart and geometry into one graphics score before averaging.
Relative to Gemini-3-Pro, it is on par on the temporal splits (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75.96</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76.12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>76.12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76.12</annotation></semantics></math> on average) but trails on the static ones (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="73.76" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>73.76</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">73.76</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="79.42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>79.42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">79.42</annotation></semantics></math>).
Logics-Parsing-Omni pairs a <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.1</annotation></semantics></math> B two-tower front end with a <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math> B mixture-of-experts (MoE) decoder that activates about <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> B parameters per token: fewer active parameters than our dense <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> B model, but about six times as many in total.
The contrast between static and temporal splits is consistent with encoding all modalities on a shared timeline (Sec. <a href="#S2" title="2 Model ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), whose benefit should be largest where a parse must align events in time and across modalities.
Overall, with a single encoder, Youtu-Parsing-Omni is the strongest open-weight model on OmniParsingBench, and its advantage is concentrated on the temporal splits.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Natural images.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Youtu-Parsing-Omni leads in entity localization and plain-entity recognition (Tab. <a href="#S5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 5.4 OmniParsingBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).
Knowledge recognition is weaker (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13.90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13.90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13.90</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21.39" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>21.39</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21.39</annotation></semantics></math> for Logics-Parsing-Omni), possibly reflecting our smaller total parameter budget (e.g., Logics-Parsing-Omni uses a <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math> B-A<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> B decoder).
Counting remains challenging across models, with all Count scores below <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80</annotation></semantics></math> despite strong Theme and Scene scores.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Graphics chart and geometry.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Youtu-Parsing-Omni achieves the highest chart Perception (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>97.49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.49</annotation></semantics></math>) and Overall (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>95.02</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95.02</annotation></semantics></math>) scores in the breakdown (Tab. <a href="#S5.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 5.4 OmniParsingBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>), with its clearest advantage in statistical-chart extraction.
In terms of Cognition score, our method is lower than Logics-Parsing-Omni (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92.93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>92.93</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92.93</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94.79" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>94.79</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94.79</annotation></semantics></math>), with the gap concentrated in visual-element and logical-reasoning questions. This is mainly because our captions tend to provide globalized descriptions and weaken the semantic descriptions of color and position, since such information contains limited effective content and is prone to introducing semantic errors.
For geometry (Tab. <a href="#S5.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 5.4 OmniParsingBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>), Youtu-Parsing-Omni also exceeds Logics-Parsing-Omni in Perception (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="63.14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>63.14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">63.14</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.32</annotation></semantics></math>), with gains in positioning, circle detection, and membership.
Geometric relations remain weaker in both Perception (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="46.77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>46.77</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">46.77</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64.24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64.24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64.24</annotation></semantics></math>) and Cognition (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76.45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>76.45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76.45</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.35" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>86.35</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.35</annotation></semantics></math>).
Together, these results suggest that richer descriptions of graphical elements and their relationships could improve how the parses support downstream questions.</p>
</div>

<span id="S5.T8.8.1.1.1.1.1.1.5.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">83.56</span>

<section id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Audio.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Youtu-Parsing-Omni’s lead over Logics-Parsing-Omni comes from more accurate temporal localization and event keywords, with gains of <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13.1</annotation></semantics></math> points, respectively (Tab. <a href="#S5.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ Graphics chart and geometry. ‣ 5.4 OmniParsingBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>).
These improvements compensate for an ASR score of <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="77.94" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>77.94</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">77.94</annotation></semantics></math>, the lowest among the compared models, revealing a stronger ability to locate and describe acoustic events than to transcribe speech relative to the baselines.
With Cognition close to Logics-Parsing-Omni (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92.39" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>92.39</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92.39</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92.94" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>92.94</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92.94</annotation></semantics></math>), the highest Overall score (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78.08" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>78.08</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78.08</annotation></semantics></math>) is chiefly supported by these perceptual gains.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T11" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T11.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 11</span>: </span><span id="S5.T11.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="S5.T11.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with open-weight models on Video-MME-v2 without subtitles.</span>
Baseline numbers are taken from the official leaderboard <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite>.
Higher is better; <span id="S5.T11.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">bold</span> and <span id="S5.T11.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">underline</span>: best and second best in each column.
</span></figcaption>
<div id="S5.T11.8" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:341.6pt;height:90.9pt;vertical-align:-43.6pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-35.7pt,9.5pt) scale(0.8,0.8) ;">
<p id="S5.T11.8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.T11.8.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="S5.T11.8.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:413.0pt;height:110.1pt;vertical-align:-52.8pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(0.0pt,0.0pt) scale(1,1) ;">
<span id="S5.T11.8.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.T11.8.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text">
<span id="S5.T11.8.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<span class="ltx_thead">
<span id="S5.T11.8.1.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="S5.T11.8.1.1.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:5.0pt;padding-right:5.0pt;"></span>

<section id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Natural and text-rich video.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Across both natural and text-rich video settings, Youtu-Parsing-Omni achieves the best Overall performance among open-weight models by virtue of its powerful temporally grounded parsing and robust semantic preservation.
In natural videos (Tab. <a href="#S5.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Graphics chart and geometry. ‣ 5.4 OmniParsingBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>), it obtains a superior temporal localization score of <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="63.68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>63.68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">63.68</annotation></semantics></math>, outperforming Gemini-3-Pro, Logics-Parsing-Omni, and Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B by <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.21</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="29.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>29.06</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">29.06</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28.60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>28.60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28.60</annotation></semantics></math> points, respectively, while reaching the highest Cognition average of <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="93.69" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>93.69</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">93.69</annotation></semantics></math> across all baselines, with leading results in object and attribute understanding (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92.91" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>92.91</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92.91</annotation></semantics></math>), audio-visual emotion understanding (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>98.82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.82</annotation></semantics></math>), and joint-best audio-visual causal reasoning (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96.49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.49</annotation></semantics></math>).
Notably, even with a lower ASR score (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="67.80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>67.80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">67.80</annotation></semantics></math>) than Gemini-3-Pro (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>84.06</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84.06</annotation></semantics></math>), its Overall score of <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="74.18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>74.18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">74.18</annotation></semantics></math> surpasses Logics-Parsing-Omni by <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.84" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6.84</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.84</annotation></semantics></math> points and approaches the proprietary Gemini-3-Pro within only <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.64</annotation></semantics></math> points, demonstrating that accurate temporal structural parsing effectively compensates for speech transcription weaknesses and maintains high-level semantic fidelity.
In more challenging text-rich videos (Tab. <a href="#S5.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ Graphics chart and geometry. ‣ 5.4 OmniParsingBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>), the model’s advantages are further strengthened, yielding an Overall score of <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75.62" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75.62</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75.62</annotation></semantics></math> that expands the lead over Logics-Parsing-Omni to <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10.26" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10.26</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.26</annotation></semantics></math> points, driven by substantial improvements in temporal localization (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50.70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50.70</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50.70</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23.05</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23.05</annotation></semantics></math>) and speech transcription (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>76.52</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76.52</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="34.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>34.28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">34.28</annotation></semantics></math>).
It also retains the highest Cognition average (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94.60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>94.60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94.60</annotation></semantics></math>) with state-of-the-art audio information extraction (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.71" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>98.71</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.71</annotation></semantics></math>) and object understanding (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78.50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>78.50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78.50</annotation></semantics></math>), while matching the best audio-visual causal reasoning score (<math id="S5.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100.00" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100.00</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100.00</annotation></semantics></math>).
Consistent superior Cognition results across both video splits, evaluated purely based on parsed outputs, verify that our unified temporal modeling paradigm effectively preserves multimodal semantics for downstream understanding, confirming its effectiveness in achieving both temporally precise and semantically reliable video parsing.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5 </span>Video-MME-v2</h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training centered on parsing may come at the expense of the general video understanding required for question answering.
We examine this on Video-MME-v2 (Tab. <a href="#S5.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ Audio. ‣ 5.4 OmniParsingBench ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>) in the setting without subtitles. Our model receives <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> visual frames; baseline scores are taken from the official leaderboard under each system’s reported configuration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At the level of the group score, general video understanding is largely preserved.
Without a thinking mode, Youtu-Parsing-Omni performs on par with larger non-thinking models and comes within <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math> points of the <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> B thinking models.
The most comparable baseline is Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct, which is also an omni-modal model evaluated without thinking and has about six times as many total parameters; Youtu-Parsing-Omni scores higher than it on the group score and on each of the three levels.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T12" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T12.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 12</span>: </span><span id="S5.T12.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Comparison with existing specialized, general, and proprietary models on ChemOCR and PDMX-Synth.<span id="S5.T12.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Left: ChemOCR (<math id="S5.T12.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> molecules; <math id="S5.T12.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="990" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>990</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">990</annotation></semantics></math> scored after excluding <math id="S5.T12.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> invalid references).
