<tr id="S5.T12.10.6" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S5.T12.10.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T12.10.6.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">LEGATO</span><sup id="S5.T12.10.6.1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S5.T12.10.6.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">∗</span></sup><span id="S5.T12.10.6.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">  </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><span id="S5.T12.10.6.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">[</span><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a><span id="S5.T12.10.6.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">]</span></cite></th>
<td id="S5.T12.10.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T12.10.6.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">23.30</span></td>
<td id="S5.T12.10.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T12.10.6.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">25.80</span></td>
<td id="S5.T12.10.6.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T12.10.6.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">31.70</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T12.10.7" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#EDEDED;">
<th id="S5.T12.10.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span class="ltx_rule" style="width:2.0pt;height:7.4pt;position:relative; bottom:-0.8pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span><span id="S5.T12.10.7.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#EDEDED;"> <span id="S5.T12.10.7.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Youtu-Parsing-Omni</span></span></th>
<td id="S5.T12.10.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T12.10.7.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#EDEDED;">22.73</span></td>
<td id="S5.T12.10.7.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T12.10.7.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#EDEDED;">26.73</span></td>
<td id="S5.T12.10.7.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T12.10.7.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#EDEDED;">33.20</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
</figure>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">L1 score.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The level-wise results indicate that this outcome stems mainly from L1, i.e., information aggregation across frames.
For the baselines, L1 varies little with either model size or inference mode: it lies within a <math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.3</annotation></semantics></math>-point range from InternVL3.5-4B-Instruct to Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Think, and enabling thinking in Qwen3-Omni raises it by only <math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8</annotation></semantics></math> points.
Youtu-Parsing-Omni exceeds every non-thinking baseline on L1 by at least <math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> points, a margin that neither additional parameters nor thinking yields among the compared models.
We attribute this margin primarily to the parsing objective, which requires the model to locate and transcribe the visual content of each frame exhaustively and thus directly exercises cross-frame aggregation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">L2 and L3 scores.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On L2 and L3, which target temporal understanding and complex reasoning, Youtu-Parsing-Omni performs comparably to the non-thinking baselines and shows no comparable advantage.
Its gap to Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Think on these levels (<math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.9</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.8</annotation></semantics></math> points) is close to the improvement that thinking brings to Qwen3-Omni itself (<math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.1</annotation></semantics></math> points on each), whereas the same change contributes less than one point on L1.
This suggests that the remaining deficit arises from multi-step reasoning over the extracted evidence rather than from perception, and that an explicit reasoning mode, which yields a gain of similar size for Qwen3-Omni, may help close it.
It may also explain why the large lead on L1 yields only a modest lead in group score, since the group-based metric requires consistent answers across related questions, many of which involve higher-level reasoning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In short, parsing-centric training preserves general video understanding and specifically improves cross-frame information aggregation, while higher-level temporal reasoning remains limited in the absence of a thinking mode.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.6 </span>ChemOCR and PDMX-Synth</h3>

<div id="S5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">ChemOCR and PDMX-Synth test whether a general parser can emit an exact formal language (SMILES and ABC notation) rather than a plausible description, and the two benchmarks separate the systems in different ways (Tab. <a href="#S5.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ 5.5 Video-MME-v2 ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">ChemOCR.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On chemical structures, Youtu-Parsing-Omni’s advantage is in exact RDK-fingerprint agreement rather than average fingerprint similarity.
On ChemOCR, it attains the highest exact fingerprint-match rate (Tani@1.0) among the compared models, <math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>54.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54.2</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="49.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>49.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49.6</annotation></semantics></math> for DeepSeek-OCR 2, while its average Tanimoto similarity (Avg. Sim.) is marginally lower (<math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="74.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>74.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">74.6</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="74.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>74.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">74.9</annotation></semantics></math>).
A higher average fingerprint similarity does not necessarily imply that a greater number of predictions share the same fingerprint. In common scenarios, the latter is considered to be more practically meaningful, so we regard Tani@1.0 as the main metric.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">PDMX-Synth.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On typeset sheet music, Youtu-Parsing-Omni attains the lowest character error rate of all compared systems, <math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="22.73" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>22.73</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22.73</annotation></semantics></math> CER, edging out the specialized LEGATO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite> (<math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23.30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23.30</annotation></semantics></math>) and remaining second to it at the symbol and line levels (<math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="26.73" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>26.73</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">26.73</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25.80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>25.80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25.80</annotation></semantics></math> SER, <math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="33.20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>33.20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">33.20</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="31.70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>31.70</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">31.70</annotation></semantics></math> LER).
The margin over the other general systems is of a different order: the strongest of them reach <math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>54</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54</annotation></semantics></math> CER (GPT-5.6 and Gemini-3-Pro), and the remaining parsers lie at <math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>72</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>94</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94</annotation></semantics></math> CER.
Taken together, Youtu-Parsing-Omni leads every compared model on ChemOCR’s Tani@1.0 metric and matches a dedicated optical-music model in character-level transcription of typeset sheet music, far ahead of the other general systems.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.7 </span>Ablation Study</h3>

<figure id="S5.F8" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.39301v1/controlled_summary_merged.svg" id="S5.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/142;" width="476" height="142"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="S5.F8.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="S5.F8.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Encoder architecture and initialization studies.</span>
(a) General multimodal (Avg-6); (b) OCRBench; (c) BLINK; (d) LibriSpeech test-clean WER.
Blue, green, and pink denote the text-initialized unified encoder, randomly initialized unified encoder, and pre-trained SigLIP-2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib80" title="" class="ltx_ref">80</a>]</cite> and SenseVoice-small <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib81" title="" class="ltx_ref">81</a>]</cite> towers, respectively.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Having established what the checkpoint achieves, we now examine how the two ideas behind the model contribute: the text-initialized unified encoder and OSAD.
We study the two principles of the encoder (Sec. <a href="#S2" title="2 Model ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) in a setting that uses general multimodal data and no parsing data.
This setting pairs a Qwen3-4B decoder with an encoder of the Qwen3-0.6B architecture (<math id="S5.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.4</annotation></semantics></math> B without its embedding layer and LM head).
General multimodal performance is summarized by Avg-6, the mean of MMBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib82" title="" class="ltx_ref">82</a>]</cite> (English and Chinese averaged), MMStar <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib83" title="" class="ltx_ref">83</a>]</cite>, MMMU-VAL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib84" title="" class="ltx_ref">84</a>]</cite>, HallusionBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib85" title="" class="ltx_ref">85</a>]</cite>, AI2D <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib86" title="" class="ltx_ref">86</a>]</cite>, and OCRBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib87" title="" class="ltx_ref">87</a>]</cite> (scaled by <math id="S5.SS7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/10</annotation></semantics></math>).
Fig. <a href="#S5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> summarizes the two encoder studies, and App. <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Additional Encoder Ablation Curves ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a> provides additional vision and ASR curves for these runs.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Unified encoder versus separate towers.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With two thirds of the perception parameters and no second tower, a randomly initialized unified encoder trails pre-trained SigLIP-2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib80" title="" class="ltx_ref">80</a>]</cite> and SenseVoice-small <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib81" title="" class="ltx_ref">81</a>]</cite> towers by <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.3</annotation></semantics></math> points on Avg-6 at <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>300</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300</annotation></semantics></math> B Stage 1 tokens (Fig. <a href="#S5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>a).
At the same budget, it trails on OCRBench by <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="53.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>53.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">53.4</annotation></semantics></math> points (Fig. <a href="#S5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>b) but achieves a lower word error rate (WER) on LibriSpeech test-clean, <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.14</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.43</annotation></semantics></math> (Fig. <a href="#S5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>d).
Text-LM initialization substantially reduces the vision gap: at the same endpoint, the text-initialized encoder comes within <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.4</annotation></semantics></math> points of the towers on Avg-6 and surpasses them by <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="77.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>77.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">77.2</annotation></semantics></math> points on OCRBench.
These results suggest that initialization accounts for an important part of the vision gap.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Effect of text-LM initialization.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At matched training budgets, initializing the shared block from Qwen3-0.6B-Base rather than from scratch gives the encoder <em id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">a reading advantage that persists throughout the plotted range</em> (Fig. <a href="#S5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>b).
The two vision branches run identical Stage 0 and Stage 1 schedules and differ only in this initialization.
The initialized encoder leads on OCRBench at every checkpoint evaluated in both branches; at <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>300</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300</annotation></semantics></math> B tokens, its advantage is <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="130.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>130.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">130.6</annotation></semantics></math> points (<math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="767.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>767.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">767.0</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="636.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>636.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">636.4</annotation></semantics></math>).
It reaches <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="672" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>672</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">672</annotation></semantics></math> early in training, a score the scratch encoder never attains within the plotted range.
On Avg-6, the benefit is mainly one of sample efficiency: the initialized encoder reaches <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64.1</annotation></semantics></math> with half the Stage 1 tokens needed by the scratch encoder to reach a comparable score, and it leads by <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.9</annotation></semantics></math> points at <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>300</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300</annotation></semantics></math> B tokens (<math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65.37" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>65.37</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65.37</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64.48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64.48</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64.48</annotation></semantics></math>; Fig. <a href="#S5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>a).
The advantage is concentrated on reading: at the same <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>300</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300</annotation></semantics></math> B budget, the scratch encoder leads on <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> vision benchmarks, most clearly on BLINK (<math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+9.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>9.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+9.5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="52.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>52.89</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">52.89</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="43.41" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>43.41</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">43.41</annotation></semantics></math>; Fig. <a href="#S5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>c), which tests spatial and relational perception.
This dissociation is consistent with the second principle of the encoder (Sec. <a href="#S2" title="2 Model ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>): weights that already map context to symbols help perception output symbols, not reason about space.
Because parsing depends on reading more than on any other capability, this is the encoder result most relevant to our task.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Contribution of OSAD.</h5>

<figure id="S5.F9" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.39301v1/osad_progress.svg" id="S5.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/155;" width="476" height="155"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="S5.F9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">OSAD supplies <math id="S5.F9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.75</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="S5.F9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.99</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.99</annotation></semantics></math> points gained after SFT (<math id="S5.F9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="88\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>88</mn><mo mathsize="1.110em">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">88\%</annotation></semantics></math>), with positive but diminishing increments.<span id="S5.F9.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> OmniDocBench v1.6 Overall (higher is better). (a) Score after SFT, RLVR, and each OSAD round; the dashed line marks TeleOCR, the strongest other system (<math id="S5.F9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.91" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96.91</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.91</annotation></semantics></math>). (b) Gain over the preceding checkpoint.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OSAD provides <em id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">most of the improvement beyond SFT</em>, contributing <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.75</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.99</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.99</annotation></semantics></math> points gained on OmniDocBench v1.6 (<math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="88\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>88</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">88\%</annotation></semantics></math>), compared with <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.24</annotation></semantics></math> from RLVR (Fig. <a href="#S5.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ Contribution of OSAD. ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>).
Its six rounds raise the Overall score from <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95.21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>95.21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95.21</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.96</annotation></semantics></math> (Fig. <a href="#S5.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ Contribution of OSAD. ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>), with gains at every round.
This continued refinement is consistent with the self-evolving design, which refreshes supervision as the parser learns. The refinement targets <em id="S5.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">content accuracy within structured outputs</em>: a schema-valid parse can still misread words, formula symbols, or table-cell values.
OSAD provides reference-conditioned feedback at these content positions while separately supervising JSON keys and delimiters.
For pages combining text, formulas, and tables, this couples precise transcription with consistent serialization, providing direct supervision for local errors that sequence-level rewards capture only indirectly.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Parsing as a Perception Interface for Agents</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Retrieval-augmented generation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite> and tool-using agents <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite> motivate reusable interfaces between external evidence and language-model reasoning.
For multimodal inputs, this interface may consist of extracted content, visual embeddings, or grounded structured records.
ColPali <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib88" title="" class="ltx_ref">88</a>]</cite> and visual retrieval systems such as VisRAG and M3DocRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib89" title="" class="ltx_ref">89</a>, <a href="#bib.bib90" title="" class="ltx_ref">90</a>]</cite> retrieve directly from document images, while Pix2Struct <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib91" title="" class="ltx_ref">91</a>]</cite> uses screenshot parsing to learn representations for visual language understanding.
MMLongBench-Doc <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib92" title="" class="ltx_ref">92</a>]</cite> evaluates understanding across long multimodal documents, and OSWorld <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite> and TheAgentCompany <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib93" title="" class="ltx_ref">93</a>]</cite> place perception within interactive computer and workplace tasks.
These settings motivate interfaces that retain both semantic content and its source location.
OmniSchema serves this purpose through a common representation of entities, relations, and spatial or temporal anchors across documents, images, audio, and video.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Omni-Modal Parsing and Perception Encoders</h3>

<section id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Document parsing.</h5>

<div id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Document understanding spans OCR-based pipelines and models that generate structured outputs directly from images.
Donut <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib94" title="" class="ltx_ref">94</a>]</cite> established an OCR-free encoder-decoder approach, while systems such as MinerU and PaddleOCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib95" title="" class="ltx_ref">95</a>, <a href="#bib.bib96" title="" class="ltx_ref">96</a>]</cite> organize recognition and layout analysis into specialized components.
Recent parsers explore different allocations of these computations: MinerU2.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite> separates low-resolution layout analysis from high-resolution recognition; dots.ocr and MonkeyOCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">58</a>, <a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">51</a>]</cite> integrate layout and content prediction; and Youtu-Parsing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite> decodes regions in parallel from shared encoder features.
MinerU2.5-Pro and PaddleOCR-VL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib97" title="" class="ltx_ref">97</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite> further improve document parsing through data and training refinements.
GOT-OCR2.0 and DeepSeek-OCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib79" title="" class="ltx_ref">79</a>, <a href="#bib.bib71" title="" class="ltx_ref">71</a>]</cite> also emphasize visual encoding tailored to text recognition and document compression.
Our work extends this encoder-centric approach to grounded parsing across visual and auditory inputs.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Omni-modal models and structured parsing.</h5>

<div id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Omni-modal language models integrate vision and audio for multimodal understanding and generation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>, <a href="#bib.bib98" title="" class="ltx_ref">98</a>, <a href="#bib.bib99" title="" class="ltx_ref">99</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>, <a href="#bib.bib100" title="" class="ltx_ref">100</a>, <a href="#bib.bib101" title="" class="ltx_ref">101</a>]</cite>.
A common architecture uses separate vision and audio encoders, followed by fusion in the language model.
Qwen2.5-Omni, for example, uses TMRoPE to align audio and video tokens through temporal positional encoding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>.
Logics-Parsing-Omni <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite> develops an explicit omni-modal parsing framework that connects detection, recognition, and interpretation through evidence grounding, and introduces OmniParsingBench, which we adopt.
Building on this task formulation, Youtu-Parsing-Omni combines a shared output schema with a unified perception encoder, Youtu-Omni-Encoder, placing audio-visual temporal alignment and selective cross-modal interaction before the decoder.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Shared representations and unified encoders.</h5>

<div id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multimodal alignment and encoder sharing address complementary aspects of perception.
ImageBind <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib102" title="" class="ltx_ref">102</a>]</cite> aligns six modalities in a common embedding space using image-paired data.
Architectures such as VATT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>, Omnivore <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib103" title="" class="ltx_ref">103</a>]</cite>, and TVLT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite> instead explore shared Transformer computation across different combinations of visual, auditory, textual, and depth inputs.
Meta-Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib104" title="" class="ltx_ref">104</a>]</cite> and OneLLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib105" title="" class="ltx_ref">105</a>]</cite> extend parameter sharing across modalities with modality-specific input processing.
Youtu-Omni-Encoder targets grounded parsing, including native-resolution pages, with a text-initialized shared backbone and a common temporal positional encoding for audio and video.
Cross-modal attention is confined to selected layers and local windows, combining shared computation with explicit temporal interaction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Language-model initialization for perception.</h5>

<div id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Pre-trained language-model weights provide a complementary starting point to visual or contrastive pre-training.
FPT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib106" title="" class="ltx_ref">106</a>]</cite> studies transfer from text Transformers to non-text tasks, and frozen language-model blocks can enrich visual representations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib107" title="" class="ltx_ref">107</a>]</cite>.
TrOCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib108" title="" class="ltx_ref">108</a>]</cite> uses pre-trained text components for recognition, while encoder-free models such as Fuyu, EVE, and Mono-InternVL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib109" title="" class="ltx_ref">109</a>, <a href="#bib.bib110" title="" class="ltx_ref">110</a>, <a href="#bib.bib111" title="" class="ltx_ref">111</a>]</cite> process image patches within the language-model architecture.
DeepSeek-OCR 2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite> is particularly relevant: its visual encoder incorporates a Qwen2-initialized Transformer with bidirectional visual attention and causal query tokens for learned reading order.
We apply text initialization to a separate perception backbone shared by vision and audio, preserving a distinct decoder and evaluating the initialization against an otherwise identical encoder trained from scratch (Subsec. <a href="#S5.SS7.SSS0.Px2" title="Effect of text-LM initialization. ‣ 5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.7</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>Post-Training for Structured Parsing</h3>

<section id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Verifiable rewards.</h5>

<div id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Reinforcement learning extends parsing supervision from reference sequences to model-generated outputs.
GRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite> provides a group-relative optimization framework, and OCR systems instantiate task-specific rewards: olmOCR-2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite> uses programmatic unit tests, while MinerU2.5-Pro and PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 incorporate reinforcement learning into their training pipelines <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>.
Our schema-routed RLVR combines shared validity checks with task-specific content scores under one policy.
The subsequent distillation stage supplies token-level feedback for structured outputs whose heterogeneous fields are difficult to supervise with a single scalar reward.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">On-policy and reference-conditioned distillation.</h5>

<div id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training on learner-generated trajectories addresses the mismatch between reference prefixes and the states encountered at inference <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>, <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>.
GKD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite> applies teacher feedback to student-generated sequences and permits different distribution-matching objectives; MiniLLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite> develops on-policy optimization of a reverse-KL distillation objective.
A separate line of work transfers information available only during training: learning with privileged information and generalized distillation formalize this setting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, <a href="#bib.bib112" title="" class="ltx_ref">112</a>]</cite>, while context distillation internalizes the benefits of additional instructions or reasoning context <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib113" title="" class="ltx_ref">113</a>]</cite>.
OPSD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite> brings these ideas together by using the same model as teacher and student under different contexts, with reference-conditioned token targets evaluated on student rollouts.
OSAD builds directly on this construction and uses the output schema to adapt supervision to token roles, assigning different divergences to content and structure within a shared all-token objective.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Self-distillation and teacher evolution.</h5>

<div id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Born-again networks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib114" title="" class="ltx_ref">114</a>]</cite> and Noisy Student <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib115" title="" class="ltx_ref">115</a>]</cite> improve models through successive teacher-student generations, while Mean Teacher and DINO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib116" title="" class="ltx_ref">116</a>, <a href="#bib.bib117" title="" class="ltx_ref">117</a>]</cite> update a teacher through an exponential moving average of student parameters.
These approaches establish teacher evolution as a general mechanism for refining supervision.
OSAD combines periodic teacher refresh with reference-conditioned on-policy targets: the teacher remains frozen within each round, then inherits the trained student’s checkpoint for the next round.
This design couples schema-aware token supervision with a supervision source that incorporates the student’s accumulated learning, as described in Subsec. <a href="#S4.SS2.SSS3" title="4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Limitations and Conclusion</h2>

<section id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Limitations.</h5>

<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Compared with its predecessor Youtu-Parsing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>, Youtu-Parsing-Omni does not yet implement inference acceleration.
Youtu-Parsing  reuses shared encoder features across the regions of a page and applies token- and query-level parallel decoding, whereas Youtu-Parsing-Omni decodes end-to-end and autoregressively with a larger decoder.
We therefore expect its throughput on dense structured content such as tables to be lower.
We will bring parallel decoding and related acceleration techniques to Youtu-Parsing-Omni in future work.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Conclusion.</h5>

<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented Youtu-Parsing-Omni, an omni-modal parser that converts documents, images, audio, and video into structured records grounded in space and time.
Its design rests on <em id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">one encoder for every modality and one schema for every task</em>.
The encoder, Youtu-Omni-Encoder, replaces separate vision and audio towers with one text-initialized Transformer, in which visual and acoustic tokens share a space-time positional encoding and interact within short audio-visual windows.
The schema, OmniSchema, casts the outputs of all ten tasks into one grounded format, which allows a single self-evolving post-training procedure, OSAD, to use the same token-role-based objective across tasks.
Together, the two components let a single <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> B-parameter checkpoint serve all ten parsing tasks with one inference configuration.
Youtu-Parsing-Omni achieves the highest OmniDocBench v1.6 score among all compared systems (<math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.96</annotation></semantics></math>) and leads all open-weight models on OmniParsingBench (<math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75.08" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75.08</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75.08</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Data</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A1.p1.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="82.25" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 650 82.25" width="650"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,82.25) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#595959;" fill="#595959" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 82.25 L 650 82.25 L 650 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F7F7F7;" fill="#F7F7F7" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 3.04 0 L 3.04 82.25 L 650 82.25 L 650 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 16.67 12.59)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:48.42em;--ltx-fo-height:4.35em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.23em;font-size:10pt;" height="63.31" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 60.19)" width="670"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.p1.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:48.42em;">
<span id="A1.p1.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p1.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Tab. <a href="#A1.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ A.1 Document Parsing ‣ Appendix A Data ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>–<a href="#A1.T16" title="Table 16 ‣ A.4 Video Parsing ‣ Appendix A Data ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> list the annotation fields for document, natural image, audio, and video parsing, respectively.
For general-purpose data, we reuse the training data of Youtu-LLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>, Youtu-VL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>, Long-VITA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>, VITA-1.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, and VITA-Audio <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>

</span></td></tr>

</table>
</figure>
<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The document data consist of two parts: full pages for layout and content parsing, and dedicated data for specialized elements.
For full pages, public document datasets are typically annotated for a single sub-task and contain label noise, so we re-annotate them with expert models and vision-language models (VLMs).
Pages that pass consistency checks and a vote among annotators with different architectures are retained directly; of the pages on which the annotators disagree, about <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\%</annotation></semantics></math> are corrected by human experts and added back to the corpus.
Synthetic pages are rendered from layout templates of magazines, papers, textbooks, manuals, and advertisements, so their labels are exact by construction.
For specialized elements, source tables of public chart datasets <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib118" title="" class="ltx_ref">118</a>, <a href="#bib.bib119" title="" class="ltx_ref">119</a>, <a href="#bib.bib120" title="" class="ltx_ref">120</a>]</cite> are serialized to Markdown, and flowcharts, mind maps, and architecture diagrams generated from sampled graphs are serialized to Mermaid.
Molecules from PubChem <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib121" title="" class="ltx_ref">121</a>]</cite> and ChEMBL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib122" title="" class="ltx_ref">122</a>]</cite> are rendered into <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math> M pairs of images and SMILES <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite> strings, geometric figures are produced by a procedural generator with primitives and relations aligned to pixels by construction, and music scores from PDMX <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite> are converted to ABC and rendered with varied engines, fonts, and layouts.</p>
</div>
</section>

<td id="A1.T14.6.10.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T14.6.10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">global_description.scene</span></td>
<td id="A1.T14.6.10.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T14.6.10.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">image</span></td>
<td id="A1.T14.6.10.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
<span id="A1.T14.6.10.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:227.6pt;">
<span id="A1.T14.6.10.3.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="A1.T14.6.10.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Short phrase describing where the image takes place.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each image is annotated in three stages: captioning, entity verification, and localization.
We first prompt a VLM to write a short caption restricted to the subject, the scene, and the action, followed by a longer narrative conditioned on that caption and the image.
Next, a large language model (LLM) extracts the entities named in the caption and the narrative, and a second VLM checks whether each entity is visible in the image.
If any caption entity is hallucinated, the sample is discarded; hallucinated narrative entities are instead removed, the narrative is rewritten from the remaining entities, and the entity lists of the caption and the narrative are merged.
Finally, each remaining entity is localized independently by SAM-3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib123" title="" class="ltx_ref">123</a>]</cite> and by a VLM.
When the IoU of the two boxes exceeds a threshold, their intersection is kept; otherwise, an LLM selects the box whose region caption matches the entity.
The region captions, kept as <span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">content.caption</span>, and the scene phrase <span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">global_description.scene</span> are also generated by a VLM.
The text inside each box is transcribed by Youtu-Parsing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite> and by a general-purpose OCR engine; when the two transcripts disagree, the element is discarded. An empty <span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">text</span> records that neither OCR system returned text, rather than guaranteeing that the region contains none.</p>
</div>
</section>

<td id="A1.T15.6.12.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
<span id="A1.T15.6.12.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:233.3pt;">
<span id="A1.T15.6.12.3.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.T15.6.12.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Segment boundaries relative to the chunk onset (</span><span id="A1.T15.6.12.3.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">HH:MM:SS</span><span id="A1.T15.6.12.3.1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">).</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A1.T15.6.13" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A1.T15.6.13.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T15.6.13.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">global_description</span></td>
<td id="A1.T15.6.13.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T15.6.13.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">entire chunk</span></td>
<td id="A1.T15.6.13.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
<span id="A1.T15.6.13.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:233.3pt;">
<span id="A1.T15.6.13.3.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.T15.6.13.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Holistic description aggregating information across segments.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The audio data consist of in-house audiobooks, podcasts, and conversations.
Each clip is first segmented: a BEATs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib124" title="" class="ltx_ref">124</a>]</cite> tagger trained with PretrainedSED <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib125" title="" class="ltx_ref">125</a>]</cite> labels every frame with an AudioSet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib126" title="" class="ltx_ref">126</a>]</cite> class, and the resulting vocal and nonvocal regions are split into segments of at most <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math> s and packed into chunks of about <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60</annotation></semantics></math> s, each of which forms one training sample.
Speech is then attributed and transcribed: DiariZen <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib127" title="" class="ltx_ref">127</a>]</cite> assigns clip-level speaker identities, three ASR systems with different architectures transcribe each turn, and the transcript with the smallest total pairwise WER is retained, while the largest pairwise WER is recorded as a disagreement score.
The language of each segment is identified from the transcript by fastText <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib128" title="" class="ltx_ref">128</a>]</cite> and from the audio by MMS-LID <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib129" title="" class="ltx_ref">129</a>]</cite>, and word timestamps are obtained by MMS forced alignment.
The timbre, delivery, and environment captions (<span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">timbre_caption</span>, <span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">instruct_caption</span>, and <span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">env_caption</span>) are generated by an audio-language model, and the scene caption and the chunk-level <span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">global_description</span> by an LLM.
For fine-tuning, a chunk is retained only if the two language identifiers agree and its disagreement score does not exceed <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math>.
For reinforcement learning, we further discard chunks whose four offline rollouts receive uniformly high, uniformly low, or identical scores from an audio-language judge; this judge is used only for this offline filtering, and online training uses the rule-based verifiable reward of Equ. <a href="#S4.E2" title="In 4.2.2 Schema-Routed RLVR ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>

<span id="A1.T16.6.10.4.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="A1.T16.6.10.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Speaker identifier, consistent across the video.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>

<td id="A1.T16.6.14.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T16.6.14.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">video</span></td>
<td id="A1.T16.6.14.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T16.6.14.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">shared</span></td>
<td id="A1.T16.6.14.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
<span id="A1.T16.6.14.4.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:159.3pt;">
<span id="A1.T16.6.14.4.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="A1.T16.6.14.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Markdown report of text-centric content for text-rich video; an empty string (</span><span id="A1.T16.6.14.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">""</span><span id="A1.T16.6.14.4.1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">) for natural video.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each video is first segmented by a VLM, at event and scene changes for natural video and at slide, page, and interface transitions for text-rich video.
The VLM then annotates the visual fields of each segment; in parallel, an ASR system transcribes the corresponding audio, a speaker diarization model assigns speaker IDs that remain consistent across the entire video, and an acoustic event tagger labels its acoustic events; the visual and audio annotations are aligned only through the segment timestamps.
Finally, an LLM summarizes the segments into the <span id="A1.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">global_description</span> and, for text-rich video, into the <span id="A1.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">structured_report</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Encoder paradigms of representative parsers.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tab. <a href="#A2.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ Encoder paradigms of representative parsers. ‣ B.1 Model Specification ‣ Appendix B Architecture Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> compares the perception front ends of representative parsers: every other parser in the table uses a separate encoder per modality, whereas Youtu-Parsing-Omni covers all three modalities with one encoder.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T18" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A2.T18.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 18</span>: </span><span id="A2.T18.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Every other representative parser uses a separate encoder per modality, and only Logics-Parsing-Omni covers all three modalities, with two towers; Youtu-Parsing-Omni covers them with one encoder.<span id="A2.T18.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
<em id="A2.T18.8.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Modality-specific</em>: every modality has its own encoder; <em id="A2.T18.8.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Unified</em>: one encoder with shared weights for all modalities.
<em id="A2.T18.8.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">End-to-end</em>: a page or clip is parsed in one forward pass rather than by a layout-then-recognition pipeline.
</span></span></figcaption>
<div id="A2.T18.9" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:62.7pt;vertical-align:-30.3pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-190.5pt,34.6pt) scale(0.475245137290735,0.475245137290735) ;">
<table id="A2.T18.9.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A2.T18.9.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T18.9.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.5pt;padding-right:3.5pt;"></td>
<th id="A2.T18.9.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.5pt;padding-right:3.5pt;"></th>
<th id="A2.T18.9.1.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.5pt;padding-right:3.5pt;" colspan="2"><span id="A2.T18.9.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Perception</span></th>
<th id="A2.T18.9.1.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.5pt;padding-right:3.5pt;"></th>
<th id="A2.T18.9.1.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.5pt;padding-right:3.5pt;" colspan="5"><span id="A2.T18.9.1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Parsing capability</span></th>
