</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Youtu-Omni-Encoder</h3>

<section id="A2.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.1 </span>Modality Stems</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both stems are thin: they only turn raw signals into tokens of the shared-block width <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> and together hold less than <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the encoder parameters.
The <em id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">vision stem</em> is a single linear map from each <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16\times 16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16\times 16</annotation></semantics></math> patch, taken at native resolution under a token budget <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>, to one token, with no convolution, absolute position table or class token, so all spatial information enters through RoPE (Subsec. <a href="#S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" title="One positional encoding for all modalities. ‣ 2.2 Unified Positional Encoding and Audio-Visual Fusion ‣ 2 Model ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>).
The <em id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">audio stem</em> applies three <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\times 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times 3</annotation></semantics></math>, stride-2 convolutions with GELU to the log-mel spectrogram, so each <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> s window of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> mel frames becomes <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lceil 100/8\rceil=13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌈</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌉</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lceil 100/8\rceil=13</annotation></semantics></math> tokens, i.e., <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math> audio tokens per second.
It then folds the remaining frequency bins into the channels and projects them to width <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> with a bias-free linear map, so that audio tokens have exactly the layout the shared block expects.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.2 </span>Shared Transformer Block</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The shared block is a standard bias-free pre-norm Transformer (RMSNorm <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>, SwiGLU FFN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>, grouped-query attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite> with QK-Norm <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>]</cite>) without a final normalization layer, since the merger supplies its own.
It departs from a language-model decoder in two ways: attention is bidirectional, and rotary embeddings are read from a per-token angle matrix, which makes the axis-factorized scheme of Subsec. <a href="#S2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" title="One positional encoding for all modalities. ‣ 2.2 Unified Positional Encoding and Audio-Visual Fusion ‣ 2 Model ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> expressible and lets the same token be rotated differently in different layers on the video path (Subsec. <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Unified Positional Encoding and Audio-Visual Fusion ‣ 2 Model ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.3 </span>Positional Encoding</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Sharing one block across modalities makes positional encoding the central design question: a single frequency budget of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{rot}}=d_{h}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>rot</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{rot}}=d_{h}/2</annotation></semantics></math> rotary slots, with <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{h}</annotation></semantics></math> the per-head dimension of the shared block, has to express 2D image geometry, 1D audio time and, for fused video, the correspondence between the two.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A plain 2D-vision / 1D-audio RoPE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite> would place video frames and their audio under incomparable positional encodings, with no frame index and with audio time occupying the slots that vision uses for height.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Chunked axis-factorized RoPE.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We instead partition the rotary budget across a set of semantic axes <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math>: each axis <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A\in\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A\in\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> receives a contiguous segment of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{A}</annotation></semantics></math> slots with its own inverse-frequency table, and the angle row <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\Phi}[s]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚽</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\Phi}[s]</annotation></semantics></math> of token <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> concatenates the per-axis contributions:</p>
<table id="A2.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\boldsymbol{\Phi}[s]=\big\|_{A\in\mathcal{A}}\ x^{(A)}_{s}\,\boldsymbol{\phi}^{(A)},\qquad\phi^{(A)}_{k}=b_{A}^{-\,k/d_{A}},\ \ k=0,\dots,d_{A}-1,\qquad\sum_{A\in\mathcal{A}}d_{A}=d_{\mathrm{rot}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚽</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><msub><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="1.200em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><msup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msubsup><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo rspace="0.392em">−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="2.000em">,</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>rot</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\Phi}[s]=\big\|_{A\in\mathcal{A}}\ x^{(A)}_{s}\,\boldsymbol{\phi}^{(A)},\qquad\phi^{(A)}_{k}=b_{A}^{-\,k/d_{A}},\ \ k=0,\dots,d_{A}-1,\qquad\sum_{A\in\mathcal{A}}d_{A}=d_{\mathrm{rot}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{(A)}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{(A)}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is the position index of token <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> along axis <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{A}</annotation></semantics></math> its rotary base.
Because each segment is normalized by its own width <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{A}</annotation></semantics></math>, every axis spans the full frequency range regardless of how many slots it owns.
Youtu-Parsing-Omni uses <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}=\{T,H,W\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}=\{T,H,W\}</annotation></semantics></math> with a common base and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(d_{T},d_{H},d_{W})=(21,21,22)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>22</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(d_{T},d_{H},d_{W})=(21,21,22)</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{rot}}=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>rot</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{rot}}=64</annotation></semantics></math> (Fig. <a href="#S2.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Stems. ‣ 2.1 Youtu-Omni-Encoder ‣ 2 Model ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>); vision tokens take <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> from the frame index and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(h,w)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(h,w)</annotation></semantics></math> from the patch grid, while audio tokens take <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> from the time offset and set <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h=w=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h=w=0</annotation></semantics></math>, so both modalities share one time axis (Subsec. <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Unified Positional Encoding and Audio-Visual Fusion ‣ 2 Model ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Unused variants.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The formulation admits two variants that the final model does not use.
First, an explicit <em id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">modality</em> axis <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> with a categorical positional encoding (image, audio, video frame, video audio) gave no gain with <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{M}=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{M}=4</annotation></semantics></math> in preliminary runs, since the two stems already produce readily separable features.
Second, an <em id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">interleaved</em> layout, in the style of the interleaved M-RoPE of Qwen3-VL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib63" title="" class="ltx_ref">63</a>]</cite>, lets <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> share one full-length frequency table through a stride-3 assignment, so that each axis covers the whole spectrum without per-axis renormalization.
Because the per-axis normalization of Equ. <a href="#A2.E7" title="In Chunked axis-factorized RoPE. ‣ B.2.3 Positional Encoding ‣ B.2 Youtu-Omni-Encoder ‣ Appendix B Architecture Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> already gives every axis the full frequency range, the two layouts differ only in where each axis samples that range; the interleaved variant is a drop-in replacement, but preliminary runs favored the chunked layout for videos of up to <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> frames. Stage 3 training uses up to <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>512</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512</annotation></semantics></math> frames, while inference uses <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> frames.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.4 </span>Token Merger and Projector</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Down-sampling acts <em id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">after</em> the shared block, so attention runs at full resolution while the decoder receives fewer tokens.
Vision tokens are merged by concatenating each <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 2</annotation></semantics></math> block within a frame along the feature axis (<math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times</annotation></semantics></math> fewer tokens, e.g., <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="196" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>196</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">196</annotation></semantics></math> decoder tokens for a <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="448\times 448" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>448</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>448</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">448\times 448</annotation></semantics></math> image), which is nearly free because adjacent patches are highly redundant.
Each modality then applies RMSNorm to the merged features, followed by a bias-free two-layer GELU MLP that maps them to the decoder width, so they enter the decoder as ordinary input embeddings.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Language Model</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The encoder’s tokens are consumed by a decoder that we pre-train for text.
It is a dense <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math>-layer Transformer of width <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}560" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,560</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}560</annotation></semantics></math> with multi-head latent attention (MLA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib130" title="" class="ltx_ref">130</a>]</cite>, which compresses the key-value cache for long outputs, and with 1D rotary positions of base <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.6\times 10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.6</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.6\times 10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> and a <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> k context.
Its pre-training follows the recipe of Youtu-LLM-2B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>, scaled to <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.5</annotation></semantics></math> B parameters.
The decoder retains 1D positions because the encoder already encodes spatial and temporal structure; this lets us reuse the text checkpoint and its long-context recipe unchanged.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Post-Training Details</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A3.p1.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="48.35" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 650 48.35" width="650"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,48.35) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#595959;" fill="#595959" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 48.35 L 650 48.35 L 650 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F7F7F7;" fill="#F7F7F7" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 3.04 0 L 3.04 48.35 L 650 48.35 L 650 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 16.67 11.89)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:48.42em;--ltx-fo-height:1.95em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" height="29.4" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 26.98)" width="670"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A3.p1.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:48.42em;">
<span id="A3.p1.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p1.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This appendix supplements Subsec. <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> with reward implementation, rollout sampling, distributed loss reduction, and the six-round training schedule.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Schema-Routed RLVR</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The reward in Equ. <a href="#S4.E2" title="In 4.2.2 Schema-Routed RLVR ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> combines two factors: shared well-formedness <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega</annotation></semantics></math> and schema-specific content accuracy <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{core}_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>core</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{core}_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We describe their components below and optimize the resulting reward with GRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>, using group-mean-centered rewards as advantages.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Well-formedness (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega</annotation></semantics></math>).</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega</annotation></semantics></math> combines three components:
<em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(i) format validity</em> (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Fmt}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Fmt</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Fmt}</annotation></semantics></math>), which averages checks for decoding after repair, decoding without repair, correctly typed required fields, and absence of undeclared fields;
<em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(ii) repetition</em> (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{repeat}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>repeat</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{repeat}}</annotation></semantics></math>), which penalizes excess top-level units, repeated field-scoped <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math>-grams, and looping relative to the reference;
and <em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(iii) incomplete coverage</em> (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{under}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>under</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{under}}</annotation></semantics></math>), which penalizes shortfalls in unit counts, semantic content, and available category or temporal fields.
Each penalty takes the largest violation across its checks, with task-specific thresholds estimated from clean rollouts.
Undecodable outputs and outputs without a primary payload receive zero reward.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Content accuracy (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{core}_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>core</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{core}_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math>).</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The content factor combines a grounded-field score <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math> with a description score <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math>.
When the reference includes descriptions, <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{core}_{\nu}=(\Pi_{\nu}+\Gamma_{\nu})/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>core</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{core}_{\nu}=(\Pi_{\nu}+\Gamma_{\nu})/2</annotation></semantics></math>; otherwise, <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{core}_{\nu}=\Pi_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>core</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{core}_{\nu}=\Pi_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For the document and image tasks used in RLVR, the grounded-field scorer is selected as follows:
<em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(i) charts and flowcharts</em> use RMS-<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and Mermaid <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively (App. <a href="#A4.SS1.SSS3" title="D.1.3 OmniParsingBench ‣ D.1 Metric Definitions ‣ Appendix D Evaluation Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1.3</span></a>);
<em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(ii) documents</em> average sequence similarity over reference-present text, formula, table, and reading-order categories;
<em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(iii) natural images</em> combine entity text similarity and box IoU with weights <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math>, renormalized over available annotations;
and <em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(iv) other structured fields</em> use sequence similarity for geometric expressions and normalized SMILES, and text similarity for OCR and music transcriptions.
The description score <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math> averages text similarity over reference-present descriptive fields.
For both entity and description scoring, text similarity is the mean of token-set <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and normalized character-sequence similarity after lowercasing and whitespace normalization. This training reward is distinct from the LLM-judged CaptionQA accuracy used to evaluate Cognition on OmniParsingBench (App. <a href="#A4.SS1.SSS3" title="D.1.3 OmniParsingBench ‣ D.1 Metric Definitions ‣ Appendix D Evaluation Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

compute the all-token and role-specific terms of </span><math id="alg1.l9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{row}}(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathsize="0.900em">ℒ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">row</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">y</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{row}}(y)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg1.l9.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span id="alg1.l9.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;float:right;"><math id="alg1.l9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> Subsec. <a href="#S4.SS2.SSS3" title="4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2.3</span></a>

<div id="alg1.l10" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l10.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">10:</span></span>
              
              
            <span id="alg1.l10.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">   update the adapters on the global objective </span><math id="alg1.l10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=N^{-1}\sum_{y\in\mathcal{B}^{+}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{row}}(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathsize="0.900em">ℒ</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">y</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathsize="0.900em">ℬ</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo></msup></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathsize="0.900em">ℒ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">row</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">y</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=N^{-1}\sum_{y\in\mathcal{B}^{+}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{row}}(y)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg1.l10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> with learning rate </span><math id="alg1.l10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">η</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{r}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg1.l10.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l11" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l11.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">11:</span></span>
              
              
            <span id="alg1.l11.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">  </span><span id="alg1.l11.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">end</span><span id="alg1.l11.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span id="alg1.l11.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">for</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l12" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l12.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">12:</span></span>
              
              
            <span id="alg1.l12.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">  merge the learned adapters into the student base weights to obtain </span><math id="alg1.l12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{r}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg1.l12.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l13" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l13.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">13:</span></span>
              
              
            <span id="alg1.l13.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">  </span><math id="alg1.l13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\theta}_{r+1}\leftarrow\operatorname{stopgrad}(\theta_{r})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">stopgrad</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></msub><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\theta}_{r+1}\leftarrow\operatorname{stopgrad}(\theta_{r})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg1.l13.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">

</div>
<div id="alg1.l14" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l14.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">14:</span></span>
              
              
            <span id="alg1.l14.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">end</span><span id="alg1.l14.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span id="alg1.l14.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">for</span>

              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l15.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">15:</span></span>
              
              
            <span id="alg1.l15.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">return</span><span id="alg1.l15.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><math id="alg1.l15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">K</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{K}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg1.l15.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">

</div>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Starting from the RLVR checkpoint, OSAD replaces sequence-level rewards with the token-level supervision defined in Subsec. <a href="#S4.SS2.SSS3" title="4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2.3</span></a>.
Alg. <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ C.2 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ Appendix C Post-Training Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> summarizes the training loop; below we specify its sampling, batch reduction, and round schedule.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sampling and loss reduction.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We sample one response per query with sampling temperature <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathrm{samp}}=0.35" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>samp</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.35</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathrm{samp}}=0.35</annotation></semantics></math>, nucleus cutoff <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.9</annotation></semantics></math>, and top-<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=50</annotation></semantics></math>. This sampling temperature is distinct from the distillation temperatures in Equ. <a href="#S4.E3" title="In Token-adaptive on-policy supervision. ‣ 4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and Equ. <a href="#S4.E4" title="In Token-adaptive on-policy supervision. ‣ 4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.
The admission gate then admits a response to the loss only if it passes JSON-validity, schema-conformance, box-syntax, and repetition checks; rejected rollouts are masked in place rather than repaired.
To make the global averaging in Equ. <a href="#S4.E5" title="In Token-adaptive on-policy supervision. ‣ 4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> explicit, let <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{k}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{k}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> be the admitted rollout instances on data-parallel rank <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, with count <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{k}=|\mathcal{B}_{k}^{+}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{k}=|\mathcal{B}_{k}^{+}|</annotation></semantics></math> and loss sum <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{k}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal{B}_{k}^{+}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{row}}(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>row</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{k}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal{B}_{k}^{+}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{row}}(y)</annotation></semantics></math>. For a nonzero global count <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=\sum_{k}n_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=\sum_{k}n_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, the objective is</p>
<table id="A3.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=\frac{\sum_{k}s_{k}}{N}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mi>N</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=\frac{\sum_{k}s_{k}}{N}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This is a mean over admitted instances, not an unweighted mean of per-rank means when admission counts differ. A rank with no admitted rollout contributes zero to both sums in this expression. An update is skipped only when <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Round schedule.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The first round starts from the RLVR checkpoint; subsequent rounds use the preceding student’s checkpoint according to Equ. <a href="#S4.E6" title="In Self-evolution through teacher refresh. ‣ 4.2.3 OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation ‣ 4.2 Post-Training ‣ 4 Training ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.
The content and structure weights <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha_{c},\alpha_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha_{c},\alpha_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> are <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0.50,0.10)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.50,0.10)</annotation></semantics></math> in round 1, <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0.60,0.10)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.60</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.60,0.10)</annotation></semantics></math> in round 2, and <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0.80,0.08)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.80</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.08</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.80,0.08)</annotation></semantics></math> in rounds 3–6, progressively emphasizing content supervision.
The learning rate is <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 10^{-7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 10^{-7}</annotation></semantics></math> for rounds 1–2 and <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.5\times 10^{-7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.5\times 10^{-7}</annotation></semantics></math> for rounds 3–6.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Evaluation Details</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A4.p1.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="46.62" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 650 46.62" width="650"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,46.62) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#595959;" fill="#595959" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 46.62 L 650 46.62 L 650 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F7F7F7;" fill="#F7F7F7" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 3.04 0 L 3.04 46.62 L 650 46.62 L 650 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 16.67 11.89)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:48.42em;--ltx-fo-height:1.83em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" height="27.67" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 25.25)" width="670"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A4.p1.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:48.42em;">
<span id="A4.p1.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p1.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This appendix defines the metrics of every benchmark, describes the evaluation toolkit we implement for OmniParsingBench, and lists the resulting evaluation set.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Metric Definitions</h3>

<section id="A4.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.1.1 </span>OmniDocBench</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OmniDocBench v1.6 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite> evaluates document parsing on pages annotated with text blocks, formulas, tables, and reading order.
We follow the official evaluation: each output is converted to Markdown, and the official pipeline matches predicted and reference text blocks, formulas, and tables one-to-one before computing the metrics below.
Text Edit is the normalized edit distance between matched predicted and reference text.
CDM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib131" title="" class="ltx_ref">131</a>]</cite> renders the predicted and reference <span id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_LaTeX_logo" style="letter-spacing:-0.2em; margin-right:0.1em;">L<span id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="position:relative; bottom:0.4ex;font-variant:small-caps;;">a</span>T<span id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="position:relative; bottom:-0.2ex;font-variant:small-caps;font-size:120%;">e</span>X</span> formulas and reports the character-level <math id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> of the rendered images.
TEDS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib132" title="" class="ltx_ref">132</a>]</cite> is a similarity based on the tree edit distance between the predicted and reference HTML tables, and TEDS-S ignores cell text.
Reading Order Edit is the normalized edit distance between the predicted component order and the ground-truth reading order.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.1.2 </span>PureDocBench</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">PureDocBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> evaluates the robustness of document parsing to image degradation.
Every page is generated from an HTML/CSS source, which also provides the structured ground truth, and is rendered in three matched versions: a clean rendering, a digitally degraded version, and a physically recaptured version (printed on paper and photographed).
Because the three tracks share identical content and reference answers, score differences isolate the effect of the image condition.
All component metrics—Text Edit, Formula CDM, Table TEDS, and Reading Order Edit—are computed exactly as on OmniDocBench (App. <a href="#A4.SS1.SSS1" title="D.1.1 OmniDocBench ‣ D.1 Metric Definitions ‣ Appendix D Evaluation Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1.1</span></a>), with Overall defined per track as the mean of <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1-\text{Text Edit})\cdot 100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mtext>Text Edit</mtext></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1-\text{Text Edit})\cdot 100</annotation></semantics></math>, Formula CDM, and Table TEDS; Avg<sub id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sub">3</sub> is the mean of the three track Overalls.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.1.3 </span>OmniParsingBench</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OmniParsingBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite> evaluates structured parsing on five splits: natural images, graphics (charts and geometric figures), audio, natural video, and text-rich video.
Each split is scored by two components.
<em id="A4.SS1.SSS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Perception</em> measures the accuracy of the grounded fields of a parse, such as localization, element extraction, OCR, and ASR, against the ground truth.
<em id="A4.SS1.SSS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Cognition</em> is measured by multiple-choice questions (CaptionQA) that an LLM judge answers by reading only the parse. Dimension accuracies are aggregated using the split-specific rules below; text-rich video first averages dimensions within the parsing and report groups, then averages the two group scores.
We use Qwen3-235B-A22B for all LLM judging in this benchmark, including Cognition and model-based Perception grader components.
<em id="A4.SS1.SSS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Overall</em> is the mean of Perception and Cognition multiplied by the post-repair parse rate.
Because the benchmark is released without a complete evaluation toolkit, we implement these metrics following the benchmark definitions.
Before scoring, every output is converted to a common representation and schema repair is applied. Outputs that remain unparseable are excluded from the component metrics and penalized through the parse rate; successfully repaired outputs are included.
For each task <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, let the parse rate <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> be the fraction of outputs that are parseable after repair if necessary:</p>
<table id="A4.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}=\frac{N_{\mathrm{parsed},t}}{N_{\mathrm{total},t}},\qquad O_{t}=r_{t}\,\frac{P_{t}+C_{t}}{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>parsed</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>total</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}=\frac{N_{\mathrm{parsed},t}}{N_{\mathrm{total},t}},\qquad O_{t}=r_{t}\,\frac{P_{t}+C_{t}}{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Natural image.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Perception evaluates the localization and recognition of three kinds of targets: plain entities, knowledge entities, and text regions.
Predicted and reference targets of each kind are matched separately by the Hungarian algorithm at IoU <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.
The identity of each matched entity is then verified by an LLM judge, and a matched text region is counted as correct when its normalized similarity exceeds <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math> or when the judge finds the reference text in the caption.
Each Perception component is the recall after these checks.
Cognition covers the dimensions <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{img}}=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>img</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{img}}=</annotation></semantics></math> {theme, emotion, scene, count, attributes, location, text, style, composition}:</p>
<table id="A4.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{img}}=\operatorname{Avg}(p_{\mathrm{plain}},p_{\mathrm{knowledge}},p_{\mathrm{text}}),\quad C_{\mathrm{img}}=\operatorname{Avg}_{d\in\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{img}}}c_{d},\quad O_{\mathrm{img}}=r_{\mathrm{img}}\operatorname{Avg}(P_{\mathrm{img}},C_{\mathrm{img}})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>img</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Avg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>plain</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>knowledge</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>text</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>img</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Avg</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>img</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>img</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>img</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>Avg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>img</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>img</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{img}}=\operatorname{Avg}(p_{\mathrm{plain}},p_{\mathrm{knowledge}},p_{\mathrm{text}}),\quad C_{\mathrm{img}}=\operatorname{Avg}_{d\in\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{img}}}c_{d},\quad O_{\mathrm{img}}=r_{\mathrm{img}}\operatorname{Avg}(P_{\mathrm{img}},C_{\mathrm{img}}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Graphics.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Charts and geometric figures are scored separately and then averaged.
For charts, RMS-<math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib133" title="" class="ltx_ref">133</a>]</cite> scores statistical charts by optimally matching table entries on header and value similarity, and Mermaid <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> scores structural diagrams by averaging the <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> of labeled nodes and labeled edges.
Chart Cognition covers OCR and data, visual elements, and logical reasoning:</p>
<table id="A4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For geometric figures, predictions are canonicalized and scored on positioning, existence of primitives, and relations, and geometry Cognition covers basic elements, geometric relations, and quantitative relations:</p>

<section id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Audio.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Perception combines segmentation, event labeling, and transcription.
Predicted and reference segments are matched one-to-one by temporal IoU, and Time <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> is averaged over the IoU thresholds <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0.3,0.5,0.7\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0.3,0.5,0.7\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Key <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> compares the event labels of overlapping segments.
The concatenated transcript is scored by WER or CER, which is converted to a score by <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{asr}}=100\,\big(1-\min(1,e_{\mathrm{asr}})\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>asr</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>asr</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{asr}}=100\,\big(1-\min(1,e_{\mathrm{asr}})\big)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Cognition covers information extraction and recognition:</p>
<table id="A4.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{audio}}=\operatorname{Avg}(p_{\mathrm{time}},p_{\mathrm{key}},p_{\mathrm{asr}}),\quad C_{\mathrm{audio}}=\operatorname{Avg}(c_{\mathrm{info}},c_{\mathrm{recognition}}),\quad O_{\mathrm{audio}}=r_{\mathrm{audio}}\operatorname{Avg}(P_{\mathrm{audio}},C_{\mathrm{audio}})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>audio</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Avg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>time</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>key</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>asr</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>audio</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Avg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>info</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>recognition</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>audio</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>audio</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>Avg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>audio</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>audio</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{audio}}=\operatorname{Avg}(p_{\mathrm{time}},p_{\mathrm{key}},p_{\mathrm{asr}}),\quad C_{\mathrm{audio}}=\operatorname{Avg}(c_{\mathrm{info}},c_{\mathrm{recognition}}),\quad O_{\mathrm{audio}}=r_{\mathrm{audio}}\operatorname{Avg}(P_{\mathrm{audio}},C_{\mathrm{audio}}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Natural video.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Time <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and the ASR score are computed as for audio.
For Key <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, action and interaction phrases are matched semantically by an LLM, which also rates the descriptions of segment pairs at temporal IoU <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 0.5</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> to obtain <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{visual}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>visual</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{visual}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Cognition covers the dimensions <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{vid}}=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>vid</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{vid}}=</annotation></semantics></math> {object/attribute, event, emotion, audio-visual causality}:</p>
<table id="A4.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{video}}=\operatorname{Avg}(p_{\mathrm{time}},p_{\mathrm{key}},p_{\mathrm{asr}},p_{\mathrm{visual}}),\quad C_{\mathrm{video}}=\operatorname{Avg}_{d\in\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{vid}}}c_{d},\quad O_{\mathrm{video}}=r_{\mathrm{video}}\operatorname{Avg}(P_{\mathrm{video}},C_{\mathrm{video}})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>video</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Avg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>time</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>key</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>asr</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>visual</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>video</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Avg</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>vid</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>video</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>video</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>Avg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>video</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>video</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{video}}=\operatorname{Avg}(p_{\mathrm{time}},p_{\mathrm{key}},p_{\mathrm{asr}},p_{\mathrm{visual}}),\quad C_{\mathrm{video}}=\operatorname{Avg}_{d\in\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{vid}}}c_{d},\quad O_{\mathrm{video}}=r_{\mathrm{video}}\operatorname{Avg}(P_{\mathrm{video}},C_{\mathrm{video}}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>

</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Time <math id="A4.SS1.SSS3.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> is computed as for natural video, and the ASR score as for audio.
For the OCR score, repeated adjacent screens are merged, and the ordered on-screen text is scored by one minus the clipped CER:</p>
