<section id="A4.SS1.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.1.4 </span>ChemOCR</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">ChemOCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite> evaluates optical chemical structure recognition on <math id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> image–SMILES pairs before scoring exclusions.
A single predicted SMILES is extracted from each output.
Following the official evaluator of ChemVLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>, RDKit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib134" title="" class="ltx_ref">134</a>]</cite> parses the predicted and reference SMILES with <span id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MolFromSmiles</span>, creates their default <span id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">RDKFingerprint</span> bit vectors, and computes Tanimoto similarity, <math id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}=|A_{i}\cap B_{i}|/|A_{i}\cup B_{i}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∩</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∪</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}=|A_{i}\cap B_{i}|/|A_{i}\cup B_{i}|</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> are the sets of active fingerprint bits.
In practice, the official scorer excludes <math id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> samples with unparseable reference SMILES from the <math id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>-sample benchmark. On the remaining <math id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=990" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>990</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=990</annotation></semantics></math> samples, we report <math id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Avg.\ Sim.}=100\sum_{i}s_{i}/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Avg</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.667em">.</mo><mi>Sim</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Avg.\ Sim.}=100\sum_{i}s_{i}/N</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.SSS4.p1.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{Tani@1.0}=100\sum_{i}\mathbf{1}[s_{i}=1]/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Tani</mi><mi>@</mi><mn>1.0</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Tani@1.0}=100\sum_{i}\mathbf{1}[s_{i}=1]/N</annotation></semantics></math>, which measure the overall similarity and the number of perfectly correct samples, respectively.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS5" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.1.5 </span>PDMX-Synth</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">PDMX-Synth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite> evaluates full-page optical music recognition on <math id="A4.SS1.SSS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="800" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>800</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">800</annotation></semantics></math> rendered score images paired with ABC transcriptions.
Following LEGATO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, we report the normalized ABC edit distance at the character, symbol, and line levels (CER, SER, and LER).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Evaluation Set</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The camera-video subset is excluded because of annotation issues; of the remaining <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{,}874" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3,874</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{,}874</annotation></semantics></math> samples, <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="136" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>136</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">136</annotation></semantics></math> have unavailable media, which leaves <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{,}738" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3,738</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{,}738</annotation></semantics></math> (Tab. <a href="#A4.T19" title="Table 19 ‣ D.2 Evaluation Set ‣ Appendix D Evaluation Details ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a>).
No sample IDs were added, and the Cognition labels of the retained samples are unchanged.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.T19" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 19: </span><span id="A4.T19.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">OmniParsingBench sample counts within our evaluation scope.</span> Natural video counts only the general subset.</figcaption>
<table id="A4.T19.7" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A4.T19.7.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A4.T19.7.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:8.0pt;padding-right:8.0pt;"></td>
<th id="A4.T19.7.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:8.0pt;padding-right:8.0pt;"><span id="A4.T19.7.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Natural image</span></th>
<th id="A4.T19.7.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:8.0pt;padding-right:8.0pt;"><span id="A4.T19.7.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Graphics</span></th>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A5.p1.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="32.78" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 650 32.78" width="650"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,32.78) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#595959;" fill="#595959" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 32.78 L 650 32.78 L 650 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F7F7F7;" fill="#F7F7F7" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 3.04 0 L 3.04 32.78 L 650 32.78 L 650 0 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 16.67 12.93)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:48.42em;--ltx-fo-height:0.75em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="13.84" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 10.38)" width="670"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A5.p1.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:48.42em;">
<span id="A5.p1.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p1.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This section provides additional vision and ASR training curves for the two encoder studies in Subsec. <a href="#S5.SS7" title="5.7 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.7</span></a>.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A5.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ Appendix E Additional Encoder Ablation Curves ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> compares the randomly initialized unified encoder with separate pre-trained vision and speech towers.
Fig. <a href="#A5.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ Appendix E Additional Encoder Ablation Curves ‣ Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> compares text-LM initialization with training the unified encoder from scratch across vision and ASR benchmarks.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Across both figures, blue denotes the text-initialized unified encoder, green the randomly initialized unified encoder, and pink the pre-trained towers.
Circular markers indicate evaluated checkpoints, and shaded bands indicate which branch performs better between the curves.
The horizontal axis counts Stage 1 training tokens in billions.
Higher vision scores and lower ASR WER or CER indicate better performance.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F10" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.39301v1/encoder_arch_ablation.svg" id="A5.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/427;" width="476" height="427"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="A5.F10.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="A5.F10.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Unified encoder versus separate towers.</span>
Green solid curves denote the randomly initialized unified encoder (<math id="A5.F10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.4</annotation></semantics></math> B); pink dashed curves denote pre-trained SigLIP-2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib80" title="" class="ltx_ref">80</a>]</cite> and SenseVoice-small <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib81" title="" class="ltx_ref">81</a>]</cite> towers (<math id="A5.F10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6</annotation></semantics></math> B combined) with random projectors.
Panels report individual vision benchmarks, the general multimodal average (Avg-6), and ASR error rates.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F11" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.39301v1/encoder_init_ablation.svg" id="A5.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/427;" width="476" height="427"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F11.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 11</span>: </span><span id="A5.F11.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Encoder initialization on vision and ASR benchmarks.<span id="A5.F11.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Blue solid curves denote the encoder initialized from Qwen3-0.6B-Base, and green dashed curves denote the encoder trained from scratch. Shaded bands indicate the performance gap, colored by the better-performing branch. Lower WER and CER indicate better ASR performance.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>

    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
